They have that physical attraction, and that's not the case with men.

And when we say it's not the case with men, we're talking about in general terms.

But there are exceptions to every rule.

There are exceptions to every rule!

Yani(يعني) Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) we talked about that man, he shaved his head, that’s Hijab(حجاب) for him, he put on an Imamah(إمامة), that was a Hijab(حجاب).

It is know there were two men in our history Waduhaa Al-Yeman(وضحى اليمن) and Al-Mukanna Al-Kindi(ألمُكَنَّا ألكِندي) were men would go around with their faces covered, not to cause others Fitnah(فِتْنَه).

There were so handsome, they covered their faces.

So, these are issues, you're saying: O Allah I  love you, that's why I'm doing it.

I'm doing it because I love you and I want to please you.

I want you to be pleased with me and I'm going to do it, whether I like it or not.

I'm going to do it so that you would reward me for doing it.

So that should be our approach.

On Wednesday, you talked about the importance of knowing what is and what is not Haram(حرام) in your area of business.

I work in media and one part of my job is to promote the financial section of the paper.

This links in with the Haram(حرام) system of interest.

Would this make my job Haram(حرام).?

So maybe what you're talking about is the financial section, so you'd talk about interest you'd talk about banking system, you'd talk about this and that.

Allah Ho Alam(ألله أعلم) I cannot say exactly what's the ruling is here because more would need to be known about the situation but I would say that if you feel that there's something doubt for in there.

You've learned  a lot Al-Hamdolillah(ألحمدلله) through your working through your education.

Take that with you and benefit the Muslims with it, find something in which you could serve Ummah(امة) and do that, Brothers or sisters! Try your best to work in something that benefits the Ummah(امة),

so that you at least can feel that I'm doing something that help in promoting the religion of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

You don't want to have your work life.

Absolutely separate from your religious life.

You want to have the two linked, correlate, so that you feel that spending these hours and hours every day is something that is pleasing Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ,

always try to make that combination.

We have to pay Zakah(زكوة) on debt that you still have at this current moment in time is a value greater than Nisaab(نصاب).

If you borrow money from me, I need to pay Zakah(زكوة) on it not you.

The one who lends pays the Zakah(زكوة), not the one, who borrows.

That's the rule.

Except if they say, Except if the debt you gave it to somebody who ripped you off and you don't expect that he's gonna pay it back to you.

In this situation you do not pays Zakah(زكوة) on it.

If you expect to pay back, you have to pay Zakah(زكوة) every year.

If you're not expecting the money back, then you do not pay Zakah(زكوة) on it.

However if you do get it back, then you pay Zakah(زكواة) on all of the past years.

So that's the ruling.

When did Umar(عُمَر) sleep and for how long.?

Allah Ho Alam(ألله أعلم) you know, many of the personal details we don't know for sure he didn't sleep a lot, he didn't sleep a lot.

But we don't know exactly when he would sleep.

IT SHUDDERS IN PAIN FREELY MY CHASITY, MY MODESTY!

OH MUSLIM, YOU SAW MY INJURY AND THE INJURY OF MY PRIDE
parts.arabic:
نَسْعَلُ اللهَ عَزُّوْاَجَلْ أَلَّا يَدَعْ بَيْنَ نَا وَلَا فِيْنَا،، اَحَدً اِلَّا بِذَنْبٍ مَغْفُوْرْ وَسَاعٍ مَشْكُوْرْ وَنَسْعَلُ اللهَ عَزُّوْاَجَلْ أَنْ َيَجْعَلَنَامِنْ كُلِّ هَماٍ فَرَجَا وَمِنْ كُلِّ ضِيْقٍ مَخْرَجَا وَمِنْ كُلِّ عُسْرٍيُسْرَاَ

نِعْمَتِ الْبِدْعَةْ هَذِهِ، اَوْ نِعْمَ الْبِدْعَ هَذِهِ أَمَّا بَعْدََ فَإِنَه’ لَمْ يَخْفَ عَلَيَّ مَكَانَكُمْ وَلَكِنِّيْ خَشِيْتُ أَنْ تُفْرَضَ عَلَيْكُمْ فَتَعْجَزُوْا عَنْهَا

كَيْفَ يَعْنِيْنِيْ شَئْنُ الرَّعِيَّهْ إِذَا لَمْ يَمَسَّنِيْ مَا يَمَسُّهُمْ كُنَّا نَقُوْلُ لَوْ لَمْ يَرْفَهْ الله عزوجل اَلْمَحَلَّهْ عَامَ الرَّمَادَهْ

لَظَنَنَّا أَنَّا عُمر يَمُوْتُوْ هَمًّا بِاَمْرِالْمُسْلِمِيْنَ بَخِنْ بَخِنْ  اِبْنِ اَمِيْرُ الْمُومِنِيْنَ يَأْ كُلُوْ بِتِّيْخَ أَللَّهُمَّ حَبِّبْ إِلَيْنَا الْمَدِيْنَهْ كَحُبِّنَا المَكَّهْ أَوْ أَشَدَّ حُبَّا

لَمَّا كَانَ عَامِ الرَّمَادَةْ قَدِمَ عُمر عَلى قَوْمِيْ وَهُمْ مِئَةْ بَيْتَ، فَنَزَلُوا الْجَبَّانَةْ فَكَانَ عُمر: يُطْعِمُ النَاسَ مَنْ جَاءَه’ وَمَنْ لَّمْ يَأْتِ أَرْسَلَ اِلَيْهِ الدَّقِيْقَ وَالتَّمْرُ وَالْأَدْمُ إِلَى  مَنْزِلِهْ

فَكَانَ يُرْسِلُ إِلَى قَوْمِيْ بِمَا يُصْلِحُهُمْ شَهْرًا بِشَهْرَا, فَوَا غَوْثَاهْ وَا غَوْثَاهْ, أتاك الغوث اَللَّهُمُّ لَا تَجْعَلْ هَلَاكَ اُمَّتْ مُحَمَّدْاِلَى يَدِي

اَللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا كُنَّانَتَوَسَّلُإلَيْكَ بِنَبِيِّنَا ﷺفَتَسْقِيْنَا, وَإِنَّانَتَوَسَّلُ إِلَيْكَ بِعَمِّ نَبِيِّنَا فَاسْقِنَا قَالَ :يَسْقَوْنَ

لَا يُقْطَعْ فِيْ الُعِذْقِ , وَلَا عَامْ اَلسَّنَةْ اِنَّا الْاَرْضَ لله يُوْرِثُهَا مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَلْعَاقِبَةُ الْمُتَّقِيْنَ۝

قَالُوْ رَبَيْهَ الْبَيْعَ لَا نَقِيْلُوْ وَلَا نَسْتَقِيْلَ لا نقيلو ولا نستقيل إِبْتُلِيْتُمْ بِيْ وَ أُبْتَلِيْتُ بِكُمْ اَسْتَغْفِرُاللهَ وَ اَتُوْبُ اِلَيْهَ، اَسْتَغْفِرُاللهَ وَ اَتُوْبُ اِلَيْهَ، اَسْتَغْفِرُاللهَ وَ اَتُوْبُ اِلَيْهَ،

اِسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كَانَ غَفَّارًا ۝ يُرْسِل السَّمَاء عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْرَارًا۝

وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ أَنْهَارًا۝

إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ بِهَذَا الْوَبَاءْ بِبَلَدٍ(بِطَّاعُوْنِ فِيْ الاَرْضٍ) فَلَا تَقْدِمُوْا عَلَيْهِ وَإِذَا وَقَعَ(بِاالاَرْضٍ) بِبَلَدٍوَأَنْتُمْ فِيْهِ فَلَا تَخْرِجُوْافِرَارًا مِّنْه

سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكَ,أَمَّا بَعْدَ، فَإِنَّه’ قَدْ عَرَضَتْ لِيْ حَاجَةْ أُشَافِهَكْ فِيْهَا فَعَزَمْتُ عَلَيْكَ إِذَا نَظَرْتَ فِيْ كِتَابِيْ هَذَا أَلَّاتَضَعْه’ مِنْ يَدِكَ حَتَّى تُقْبِلَ إِلَيً,

يَا اَمِيْرُ الْمُو مِنِيْنَ إِنِّيْ قَدْ عَرَفْتُ حَاجَتَكَ إِلَيّْ وَإِنِّيْ فِيْ جُنْدٍ مِّنَّ الْمُسْلِمِيْنَ لَا أَجِدُبِنَفْسِيْ رَغْبَةً عَنْهُمْ

فَلَسْتُ أُرِيْدُ فِرَاقَهُمْ حَتَّى يَقْضِيْ اللهُ فِيْيَ وَفِيْهِمْ أَمْرَه’ وَقَضَاهْ , فَحَلِّلْنِيْ مِنْ عَزْمَتِكَ يا أمير المومنين وَدَعْنِيْ فِيْ جُنْدِيْ

يَا اَبَتِيْ قَالَ سَتَجِدُنِي إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ صَابِرًا وَلَا أَعْصِي لَكَ أَمْرًا۝

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ says; وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَامَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ

إِنْ كُنْتُمْ آمَنْتُمْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ۝

في مصالحل المسلمين وَاللهِ لَا يُفْتَحْ بَعْدِيْ بَلَدْ فَيَكُوْنُ فِيْهِ كَبِيْرَ نَيْلٍ بَلْ عَسَى أَنْ يَكُوْنَ كَلَّا عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِيْنَ،

فَإِذَا قَسَّمْتُ أَرْضَ الْعِرَاقِ بِعَلُوْجِهَا, وَأَرْضُ الشَّامِ بِعَلُوْجِهَا, فَمَايَسَدُّ بِهِ الثُّغُورْ؟

وَمَا يَكُوْنُ للِذُّرِّيَّةْ وَالْأَرَامِلْ لِهَذَا الْبَلَدْ وَبِغَيْرِهِ مِنْ أَرَاضِي الشَّامِ وَالْعِرَاقْ؟

فَأَكْثَرُا عَلَى عمر تَقِفْ مَا أَفَاءْ اَللهُ عَلَيْنَا بِأَسْيَافِنَا عَلَى قَوْمِ لَّمْ يَحْضُرُوْا وَلَمْ يَشْهَدُوْا, وَلأَبْنَاءِ الْقَوْمْ وَأَبْنَائِهِمْ وَلَمْ يَحْضَرُوْا

وَلَكِنْ رَّأَيْتُ أَنَّه’ لَمْ يَبْقَ شَيْء يُفْتَحْ بَعْدَ أَرْضَ كِسْرَى وَقَدْ غَنِمْنَا الله أَمْوَالَهُمْ وَأَرْضَهُمْ وَعَلُوْجَهُمْ فَقَسَّمْتُ مَا غَنَمُوْا وَمِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ بَيْنَ أَهْلِهْ

وَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ أَنْ أَحْبِسَ الْأَرْضِيْنَ بِعَلُوْجِهَا وَاضِعًا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيْهَا الْخِرَاجْ وَفِيْ رِقَابِهِمِ الْجِزْيَةْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ هَذِهِ الثَغُوْرَ لَا بُدَّ لَهَا مِنْ رِجَالٍ يَلْزَمُوْنَهَا,

أَرَأَيْتُمْ هَذِهِ الْمُدَنِ ألْعِظَامْ لَا بُدَّ لَهَا مِنْ أَنْ تُشْحِنَ بِالْجُيُوْشَ يُنْفَخُ فِيهِ الرُّوحُ الم  ۝ ذَٰلِكَ الْكِتَابُ لَا رَيْبَ  فِيهِ  هُدًى لِلْمُتَّقِينَ ۝

الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ ۝

دَيْن لأ يُرجع صَدَادُو صَلَّى الله عَلى سَيَّدِنَا محمد وَعَلى اَلِهِ وَ صَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ تَسْلِيْمًا كَثِيْرًا

parts.english:
This evening we'll talk about, the rules of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) in choosing his governors.

These are the men, who would face the people and represent Umar(عُمَر) in the various Muslim states.

In those days it would be impossible to have a centralized system.

So, it was more of a federal system, where the Muslim Khilafah(خِلَافَه) is divided into states, Wilayaat(ولايات) and every state is headed by a governor,

and that Governor has a lot of independence.

Because keep in mind that in those days, there was no telephone service, no fax service, no email forms of transportation were very slow, no planes, no cars, no trains.

So it's impossible to have a centralized system, where everything is controlled from Madina.

Therefore the choice of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) of governors was very important because these will be his representatives in establishing the law of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

So, what were the qualities that he was looking for, when he would choose a Waali(والي).

Now, the posts that existed then, was Waali(والي) and then you have a Ameer Al-Jund(اميرالجند), this is the military general, you had Qaadhi(قاضي), judge

and you had Aamil Zaka'ah(عامل زكواة), the one who collects the Zakaah(زكوة).

Sometimes these roles would be in Independent and sometimes they would be combined.

Number one, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) was searching for Al-Qawwi-Ul-Ameen(القوى الامين).

Al-Qawwi(القوي) the literal translation of it is strong but I think we talked about this concept earlier that it really means the competent,

somebody who's competent in that field.

It doesn't necessarily mean physical strength it means that you are strong in that field and also Amanah(امانة), the person needs to be trust worthy.

Shurhabeel Bin Hasanah(شُرحبيل بن حسنة), one of the Umara'a(امراء) was changed by Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) and he appointed instead of him Muawiyah Bin abi Sufiyan(معاويه بن ابي سفيان).

So, Sharhabeel(شُرحبيل) went to Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) and he said; Did you change me because I've done something wrong? You're upset with me?

I've angered you in one way or another?

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: No! That's not the reason.

But because, there is a man who's stronger than another man.

So, the reason why I changed you is because I think that Muawiyah Bin abi Sufiyan(معاويه بن ابي سفيان) is more capable of fulfilling this particular role.

Shurhabeel Bin Hasanah(شُرحبيل بن حسنة), was a good the military leader.

He was appointed in the time of Abu Bakr Siddique رضي الله عنه to lead one of the armies that were in Ash-sham(ألشام).

But in this particular post now, there might have been a civilian post, role.

He was changed and Muawiya(معاويه) replaced him and Umar رضي الله عنه, gave the justification. He said; Some men are stronger than others.

In fact, there is another story that Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) was asking, he said; Who is better Mo'min Muttaqi(مؤمن متقي) who has Taqwa(تقوى), but is weak

or somebody, who is strong.

So, the response Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) got was, the Taqwa(تقوى) of the Muslim is for himself, but his weakness would affect his subjects.

While the strength of a man would affect his subjects positively.

So, they're telling him that appointing somebody, who's strong but might have less Taqwa(تقوى) than somebody else, who's weak is better.

Now, obviously we're talking about here relative scale of Taqwa(تقوى).

We're not talking about somebody who is Fasiq(فاسق) both have Taqwa(تقوى) but one of them has more Taqwa(تقوى) than the other.

There has to be a bottom line of Taqwa(تقوى) with anybody who assumes a position of leadership.

No matter what it is!.

Umar Bin Khattab رضي الله عنه used to say; "O Allah I seek refuge in You from a strong disbeliever and a weak or incapable believer." I seek refuge in you, from a Kafir(كافر) who is  strong.

A Kafir(كافر) who's devoted to serving Shaytan(شَيْطَانْ).

Who sleeps very little and works a lot.

And I seek refuge in You, from a believer who's doing nothing.

So, make sure that you are not one of those whom Umar Bin Khattab رضي الله عنه is seeking refuge in Allah from.

It doesn't make sense to have a believer who knows the truth, who has who has Baseerah(بصيره), who has seen the light, who knows about Jannah(جنة), who knows about Hellfire

sitting down and doing nothing, a couch potato.

And then you have a Kafir(كافر) who's blind, blinded from the truth and knows nothing about the path of Shaytan(شَيْطَانْ) and is devoted and active and hard working.

How can the soldier of Shaytan(شَيْطَانْ) be better than the soldier of Ar-Rahman(الرحمن) it's a shame if that's the case.

So, make sure brother and sister that you're not one of those, because Jibreel عليه السّلام, he came to Muhammadﷺ and said; I am surprised.

Jibreel(جِبْرِيْل) is telling Muhammadﷺ, I am surprised how can somebody know about Jannah(جنة) and then not work for it?

And how can somebody know about Hellfire and then sleep and not seek refuge from it?

How could that be?

Rasool Allah ﷺ says: On the Day of Judgment if there was a person who was being pulled on his face in Duniyah(دُنِيَّا), I mean imagine, being pulled on your face.

Right! You're being dragged by a car on your face, since the day you were born until the day you die.

Rasool Allah ﷺ said: If there was somebody who was being pulled on their face, in Duniyah(دُنِيَّا), from the day they were born, until the day they were they died,

they would see that as insignificant on the day of judgment, when they face Allah.

If you suffered your entire life in the sake of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ by being dragged on your face, suffering that torment, day in and day out.

On the Day of Judgment, when you see the reality you would view.

What was done to you as insignificant? Nothing.!

" the people of Jannah(جنة) don't regret anything but a moment that passed by them and Duniyah(دُنِيَّا) and they didn't mention the name of Allah."

Number two, Experience! He was looking for experience.

He was about to assign someone to the post of a Waali(الوالي), and then they told Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) and apparently they told him, this as a praise of this man

they said this man knows no evil, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: If he doesn't know evil, then he might commit it.

And he refused to assign him to that post.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) wanted a man who was experienced, who knows about Ash-Shar(الشر), knows about evil, because if you know about it, you won't fall into it.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) was not interested in finding, what we would call today, a nerd or a bookworm, who's sitting at home, studying the books,

you know, doing all of the Shariah Ilm(شريعه علم), but doesn't know what's going on in the streets.

Because such a person would be inexperienced, he would be shocked by reality.

He has an ideal view of the world.

But Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) wants, people who, in fact, in one statement Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said; Islam will be lost when there will be people, who don't know about Jahilliyah(جاهلية).

He said: These generations that are being born in Islam and they know nothing about the slam, they don't know Jahilliyah(جاهلية), they are the ones, who would lose Islam.

Why? Because they don't know the bitter taste of Jahilliyah(جاهلية), they haven't tasted it.

Hearing about something is not like seeing it.

We can read about Jahilliyah(جاهلية).

But the ones who lived Jahilliyah(جاهلية), they're the ones who really, really, really hate it.

And that's why you would find that, an ex smoker hates the smell of cigarettes more than someone who never smoked in his life.

The smokers will testify to that, you just can't stand that smell anymore.

And I would assume maybe the same could be said about people who were former alcoholics Allah Ho Alam(الله أعلم), maybe because alcohol is different maybe sometimes

the person could have that maybe with alcohol and drugs, unless a person is very, very, very detached from it.

Maybe they could still have that addiction attachment to it, Allah Ho Alam(الله أعلم), but the thing is here that, with the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم, who grew up in Shirk(شرك)

for them Islam was everything, because Islam saved them.

But  somebody, who was born into it, might take it for granted.

So, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) is saying; If he doesn't know about Sharr(شر) if he doesn't know evil, he might be tricked into it.

So, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) is looking for people who are experienced people who cannot be tricked, who cannot be fooled, people who are not naive or gullible,

people who know the haqq(حقّ) and they know the Batil(باطل) and you cannot fool them.

Number three: And this was one of the conditions, he would never appoint a relative even if they were qualified, one of the most qualified man among the Sahabah(صحابه) was, Abdullah Ibn Umar(عبدالله ابن عمر)

and his name was brought up in many nominations and Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) would respond to them harshly.

Once he said: I want a man who has these qualities 1,2,3…..

The man said that I have him.

I know who should, who that man is, Umar(عُمَر) said: Who?

He said: Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب). He said; May Allah kill you, you don't want the face of Allah with that statement.

you just want to make me happy.

Even though the man might have been very sincere, in that suggestion.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) ruled out having any of his family assume positions of responsibility.

And the most beloved of his family to him, was Abdullah(عبدالله) and he would tell his son; O my son, it's enough for one of us, to be trialed on the Day of Judgment for being responsible for the Muslims.

It's enough for one man from the family of Umar(عُمَر) to be held accountable on the Day of Judgment for everything that happens to every Muslim.

I don't want anyone else of my family to suffer that on the Day of Judgment.

He viewed it as a responsibility that he would be asked about, he would say; If someone appoints a relative or a friend for no reason, but their relationship or friendship,

they have betrayed Allah and His Messenger.

If you appoint a relative or you appoint a friend.

And the reason why you do so, is because they are your friend or relative, then that is betraying Allah and His messenger.

So, in our organizations in our Masajid(مساجد) it in our Islamic groups, we need to make sure that the reason why we are appointing people, is not because they're from the same tribe, from the same clan,

from the same family, because he's my buddy.

They should be chosen based on the merits, based on their qualifications, because this is an Amanah(أمانة).

And a person who appoints somebody is, as the person who's responsible.

Number four: He would never appoint somebody who asked for it.

If he feels that somebody is seeking that position of responsibility, somebody who is power hungry, he would avoid him.

He would not give it to somebody who is keen to have that responsibility because, he would say; Whoever asks for this affair would not be supported by Allah in it.

If a person is appointed in a position of responsibility, then Allah will help that person but if a person asked for it, and struggles to get it then Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ will leave that person alone

and in such positions of responsibility, you definitely need the help of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

You don't want to be left on your own.

So, somebody who asked for it will not be held by Allah while somebody who does not ask for it.

And it doesn't make a difference to that person, whether their appointed or not, such a person will be given help and assistance by Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

Number six. And this is an interesting condition. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) would ban anyone who is in a position of responsibility

from being involved in trade or commerce.

If a person is a Waali(وآلي), they are not allowed to do business, he would give them a good salary, but they would not be allowed to invest any money

and get involved in business.

And Ibn Khaldoon(ابن خلدون) he talks about this concept in his book in Al-Muqaddamah(المقدمه).

And he has a long essay about this.

And what he's saying is that whenever you have a mixture of political leadership and business, business goes wrong.

When somebody who has political power gets involved in business, they would have an edge over the businessmen who are not politicians.

And that is a flaw in the equilibrium that exists in the market.

You see, Islam allows the people to do business without placing any restrictions on them except the restrictions of Shariah(شريعه).

For example, when the prices went up in Al-Madina(المدينه) they came to Rasool Allah ﷺ and said: O Rasool Ullah O Rasool Ullah make a pricing for us, to reduce the prices.

Rasool Allah ﷺ said; Allah is the One, Who sets the prices and He is the One, Who gives Ar-Rizq(الرزق) and I don't want to be held accountable on the Day of Judgment

for preventing the Ar-Rizq(الرزق) of someone from getting to him.

Rasool Allah ﷺ is saying: There's a certain equilibrium in the market.

And that equilibrium is what, determines the prices it's a supply and demand thing, that's what they say today.

Even though that's not how it was expressed in the Hadith(حديث) of Rasool Allah ﷺ but it is the same concept.

It is Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ who sets the prices.

Based on the supply and demand in the market Somtimes the prices would go up sometimes, they would go down.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ is saying: I don't want to intervene myself and set or fix the prices because I would be committing oppression, wrong against someone

either the buyer or the seller, I would be wronging in one of them.

However, when somebody who has political power gets involved in business because of that upper hand that is an advantage for that person and the marketplace,

you would find disadvantage with everybody else.

And Ibn Khaldoon(ابن خلدون)  says: That causes Fasad(فساد), it causes corruption.

So, he said that the Sultan(سلطان) and all of his workers employees need to pull their hands out of business completely and they should be paid by the Muslim Treasury a salary that is sufficient for them

and they should not be allowed to intervene in business whatsoever.

Politicians should be separate from businessmen and that was something that Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) has stated centuries before Ibn Khaldoon(ابن خلدون).

His Ummal(عمال) and Wulaa(ولآه) were prevented from doing business.

Number Six; To make sure that this rule is applied, he would make an accounting of the wealth of the Waali(وآلي) before the appointment and when he is discharged from his job.

So, he would make Muhasibah(محاسبه) accounting of every single penny that, this Waali(وآلي) has.

For example Muadh Ibn Jabal(معاذابن جبل) he would look at the wealth of Muadh Ibn Jabal(معاذابن جبل) how much does he have?

And then when he is discharged from that job, he would hold him accountable again.

Any plus, any surplus that the Waali(وآلي) would have Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) would take it away.

If he had 100,000 before he became Waali(وآلي) and then after he is discharged, he has 150, he would take that 50,000 and put it in Bait Ul-Maal(بيت المال).

Therefore according to Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) you're not supposed to leave your job with more money.

We pay your salary to make a living during that time and that's it.

You are not supposed to walk out as a millionaire.

In fact, it is said that he would command his Wulaa(ولاء) to come into Madina during daytime and not at night, so that they can't hide anything.

Number seven; He would have them sign a contract, and there would be witnesses some of the terms in the contract Barzoon(برضون), is an animal, in terms of sizes between a donkey and a horse

and it's expensive and it was used as a form of transportation for the elite.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: None of my governors are allowed to use that And they should not eat expensive food, nothing pure, nothing expensive.

And he should not wear soft clothes.

So, if you had a suit and tie and fancy clothes on, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) would not like that.

And you do not shut your door in front of any Muslim.

Anyone who has a need you need to be ready and available to respond to their needs.

So, his governors are really servants for the people.

Number eight Shura(شورى) before he would choose a Waali(والي), he would consult with the seniors Sahabah(صحابه), Uthman Ibn Affan(عثمان ابن عفان), Ali Ibn Abi Talib(علي ابن ابي طالب),

Abdur Rahman Bin Auf(عبدالرحمن ابن عوف), Az-Zubair Bin Awwam(ألزبيربن عوام) these were his close advisors, Saad Bin Abi Waqas(سعدبن أبي وقاص)

he would make Shura(شورى), before he would appoint anyone.

Number nine; If he doesn't know the Waali(والي), first hand.

He would test him, so he invited Al-Ahnaf Bin Qais(ألأخنف بن قيس) to come to Madina.

So, Al-Ahnaf Bin Qais(ألأخنف بن قيس), comes in to Madina.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) holds him in Madina.

Al-Ahnaf(ألأخنف), wants to leave and Umar(عُمَر) is holding him back.

For a full year, He had him in Madina for a full year, after this year past.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب), told Al-Ahnaf(ألأخنف).

O Ahnaf(ألأخنف), I was testing you and I found out that what appears from you is good and I asked Allah that what is inside you is even better

and O Ahnaf(ألأخنف)! We used to be told that the ones who will destroy this Ummah(امة) are the Knowledgeable Munafiqeen(منافقين).

And then he said: O Ahnaf(ألأخنف), Do you know why I held you back for a year?

It is because I want to appoint you as a governor.

So, he tested him, he would not rush to judgment, he was not spontaneous.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب), would not take a decision unless he knows exactly what he's doing, he wouldn't rush to judgment.

Sometimes, we were very fast in making assumptions.

We would see a person, we would immediately make a judgment on them even though our Farasah(فراسة) might be zero.

Hear something on the news, immediately, make a judgment, read something in the paper, immediately make a judgment, No… you  know swallow it in, sit on it, think about it, don't just follow your whims your emotions.

A Muslims should not rush into judgment especially when it is relating to information that is coming from a Fasiq(فاسق) source.

O you, who believe if a Fasiq(فاسق), a corrupt person and an untrustworthy person brings you some news verify it first.

Take the time to verify.

Number Ten: Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) would never allow himself or his governors to appoint non Muslims in any government responsibility.

None!

None, That  was a fixed rule.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب), was meeting with Abu Musa(أبوموسى).

So, he told Abu Musa(أبوموسى): Have your assistant give the report in the Masjid(مسجد).

Abu Musa(أبوموسى) said: He would not come into the Masjid(مسجد), Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: How come?

He said: Because he is Christian.

This was an assistant of Abu Musa Al Ash'ari(ابوموسى ألأشعري), Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said; Do not bring them close, when Allah has made them far away,

when Allah has distanced them from you, And do not honor them, when Allah has dishonored them.

And do not trust them, when Allah has said that they are untrustworthy.

And Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) he had a servant, his name is Ashiq(عأشِق), he said; He told his Christian servant, I want you to become Muslim.

So, that I can appoint you in some positions of responsibility because we are not allowed to seek assistance from non Muslims.

Ashiq(عاشق) said: I told Umar(عُمَر): I don't want to change my religion.

And Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) was fine with that. He said: There's no compulsion in religion.

Some of the characteristics of the men, whom umar ibn al-khattab رضي الله عنه chose.

Number one: Az-Zuhad(الزهد), All of these men were austere, they had Az-Zuhad(الزهد), they were not attached to Duniyah(دُنِيَّا), they did not love Duniyah(دُنِيَّا).

Therefore, this made them work for the sake of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ, and for Aakhira(آخرة).

They were not serving their personal interests.

You know, even though all of them were Zuhaad(زهاد), but some of them were on an even higher level, such as Saeed Bin Amir(سعيد بن عامر), Abu Musa Al Ash'ari(ابوموسى ألأشعري), Muadh Ibn Jabal(معاذإبن جبل),

Abu Obaidah Amr Bin Jarrah(أبوعبيدةعمروبن جراح), Salaman Al Farsi(سلمان الفارسي).

These among, the Sahabah(صحابه) were famous as being Zuhaad(زهاد), all of the Sahabah(صحابه) were Zuhaad(زهاد), but these were even at a higher level.

And these were all men whom Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) appointed as Wulaa(ولاه).

Number two: They  were very humble and power did not changed them.

They never changed their ways, the simple ways of the Arabs of Arabia.

They carried on living a simple life, the Romans sent a representative to meet with the Muslim Ameer(أمير) of the armies in Ash-sham(ألشام) and who was the Ameer(أمير), Abu Obaidah(ابوعبيدة),

one of the 10 given the glad tidings of Jannah(جنة).

So, this Roman representative is coming from a certain culture, where they treat, the leaders with certain respect, the way they dress is different, the way they sit is different, the way they act is different.

So, he comes in and the Muslims are just sitting on the floor.

He said: Where is your Ameer(أمير)?.

So, they pointed towards Abu Obaidah(ابوعبيدة).

He said: I came to a man he was sitting on the floor with his bow on his shoulder, and he was playing with arrows in his hand.

So, I came to him and I said; How come you're sitting on the floor?

You know, Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله), He came with a completely different mission but just he couldn't hold back asking Abu Obaidah(ابوعبيدة) this question.

He said: How come you're sitting on the floor?

Would it make you different in the eyes of Allah if you are sitting on a throne.

Abu Obaidah رضي الله عنه said: I'm going to be very honest with you and I'm going to tell you the truth.

I have no dirham(درهم) or dinar(دينار) in my pocket, I am broke you know, imagine an Ameer(أمير) telling a representative here.

And Abu Obaidah(ابوعبيدة) said: I'm going to tell you the truth, I have nothing I'm broke and I had to borrow money from my brother Muadh Ibn Jabal(معاذإبن جبل) to feed myself.

But then he said: But even if I had money enough to buy for myself a throne to sit on.

I'm not going to be a person, who would sit on the throne and have my Muslim brother sit under me on the floor, when he could be better in the eyes of Allah then myself, and then he said;

And he said: And we the servants of Allah, we walk on the floor, and we sit on the floor, and we eat on the floor, and we sleep on the floor.

And that does not reduce us in the eyes of Allah.

In fact, it raises our status in the eyes of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

So, they're very humble, simple.

And you know, that's a lesson for us, it is not your clothes that make you who you are?

It's not the way you try to act, it's not the image that you try to project, it's not the car that you drive, it is what is in your heart.

And sometimes when people put on a show, which is fake.

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ does not let them die, until he exposes them.

So, we ask Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ to give us all Sitr(ستر), to conceal our privacy's and to make our Sareerah(سريره) better than Ala-niyah(اعلانيعة).

To make the private better than the public.

So, Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ honored these Sahabah(صحابه), but the honor that he gave them was not through the clothes that they were wearing or the Barzoon(برضون) that they were riding or the throne they were sitting on.

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ honored them by putting the love of them, in the hearts of the Aoulea(أوليآء) of Allah.

Every Walli(ولي) of Allahعَزَّوَجَل loves Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب).

Every Walli(ولي) of Allah loves Abu Obaidah(ابوعبيدة), even though Abu Obaidah(ابوعبيدة) would sit on the floor because the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم understood that it's not this position of Ameer(أمير) that would give him the status.

They understood, that Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ said in Qur'an; Allah gives kingdom to whomever, He wishes and He strips it away, from whoever He wishes.

And a person could be in the utmost level of magnificence and strength and power and Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ can humiliate that person and bring him down to the lowest levels that can happen.

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ gives the kingdom to whomever He wills and He takes it away from whomever He wills.

And Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ honors.

And Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ honors whomever He wills and He humiliates, whoever He wills, and it's the destiny of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ that He will honor the believers

and He will dishonor the disbelievers and if that doesn't happen in Duniyah(دُنِيَّا) and it will happen one day, it will definitely happen on the Day of Judgment.

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ said in Qur'an and Rasool Allah ﷺ says it in the Hadith(حديث).

Let the disbelievers do whatever they want, assume whatever power they want, gather all of the money they want.

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ will expose them and Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ put them in the place that they deserve.

Everything is done in Duniyah(دُنِيَّا) is temporary and it will go.

The money of Qaroon(قارون) did not last long and the kingdom of Firaun(فرعون) did not last long and Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ humiliated both of them. ?

And the great humiliation for both of them will even be more on the day of judgment when they meet Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ and the believers who were dishonored in Duniyah(دُنِيَّا) and were persecuted and killed

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ has reserved from them, a very high status on the Day of Judgment.

Just imagine what Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ will do to the people of Ukhdood(ألأخدود) The believers who are burnt alive in the trenches.

How will Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ honor the Sahabah(صحابه) who died as Shuhadaa(شهداء)?

How will Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ honor Hamza bin Abdul Mutalib(حمزةبن عبدالمطلب).?

How will Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ honor the Qurr'aa(قراء) of Quran, who were executed by the disbelieving Arab tribes.

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ will hold them in very high status on the Day of Judgment.

And that's when everybody will be jealous with that status.

And they would have wish that they have followed that path.

So, if you don't see justice in Duniyah(دُنِيَّا), if you see a lot of unfairness in Duniyah(دُنِيَّا).

Don't be disheartened because the day of justice is the day of judgment and that's why it's called the Day of Judgment.

It is the day of judgment…. It's a day of justice....

They had Wara'a(وراع) piety and Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) had a problem with convincing some of them to be governors.

Ut'ba Bin Ghazwaan(عتبة بن غزوآن), he came to Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) and said; I don't want to be the governor over Basra(بصرى).

Find somebody else Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) refused.

Ibn Abbas(إبن عباس) when the governor of Homs(حمص) died.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) tried to convince him to become the Waali(والي) over Hims.

Ibn Abbas(إبن عباس) said: No way!

I'm no Waali(والي), I'm not going to become a Waali(والي).

Nauman Bin Maqran(نعمان بن مقرن), he comes to Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) and he said; Please discharge me from being a Waali(والي) because I want to go and fight Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله).

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) came to Az-Zubair Bin Awwam(ألزبيربن عوام) and told him; You are my governor over Egypt - Egypt! The jewel, Egypt very important government, Wealthy and huge.

Zubair(زبير) you are my governor over Egypt.

Zubair(زبير) said; I don't want to be a governor of the Egypt, I want to be Mujahid(مجاهد) Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله) and a helper of the Muslims.

That was the life they wanted to live there are not looking into infiltrating governments and becoming leaders.

They wanted to go Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله عَزَوَجَلّ) and die Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله) that was the path that they chose for themselves.

THE RESPONSIBILITIES WULAA'A(ولآة).

What were their responsibilities in those days?

Number one, the most important responsibility is to establish the Deen(دِيْن) of Allah.

Yazeed Ibn Abi Sufiyan(يزيدبن أبي سُفيان), he sends a letter to Ameer Ul-Mo'mineen(أميرالمؤمنين) and he said; Yazeed(يزيد) said: The people in the Ash-Sham(ألشام) have multiplied the population is increasing

and they are filling the towns of Ash-Sham(ألشام), and they need men to teach them Qur'an.

So, help me with men who would teach them.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) sent him five of the Fuqahaa(فقهاء) of Sahabah(صحابه).

They were very short, the Sahabah(صحابه) were very short in manpower because the number of the Sahabah(صحابه) was very low.

Nevertheless, Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله), the lands that were opened by the Sahabah(صحابه) are the lands in which not only Islam took root but the Arabic language also flourished.

Unlike the lands that were opened after the Sahabah(صحابه).

In Ash-Sham(ألشام) you have some Arab tribes living but not all of Ash-Sham(ألشام) were Arabs.

Syria, Jordan, Lebanon and Falastine(فلسطين) not all of the people were Arabs.

You have a lot of indigenous Roman people, the Arabs were scattered tribes but nowadays that's the official language of out of these four countries i.e. Arabic.

No other languages exist.

Egypt was a non Arab country, they were Coptic's and they had their own language.

Now, the Egyptians have adopted Arabic language and they became Arabs.

North Africa, you had the barber people and then some Arab tribes settled in Algeria, Tunisia, Morocco and Libya.

However, all of these countries now speak Arabic.

Al-Andalus(ألأندلس) also for 800 years the language was Arabic.

While you would find that in the time of a Taba'een(تابعين) and Taba Taba'een(تابع تابعين) Islam would take root but the language didn't go beyond that area.

So, even though the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم were very short on the human resources but Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ blessed their efforts.

Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله), we can't even imagine how much Hasanaat(حسانات) are being piled up on the scales of the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم on the DAY of JUDGEMENT

because, it goes to their credit that we are Muslim today.

They are to be credited with that.!

So, everything that we do, they receive a copy of that in their account.

In the time of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب), he built about 4000 Masajid(مساجد).

Number two: Tamaeen an-Naas(تعمين الناس), Providing peace and security to their subjects.

They would guard them, they would protect them, so peace flourished.

A Muslim could leave their shop unlocked and go to Salah(صلاة), A Muslim woman can go out and travel fearing no one.

Rasool Allah ﷺ said, in the Hadith(حديث) to Udae Bin Hatim(عدي بن حاتم) A woman would come all the way from Iraq to Makkah, fearing no one but Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) he sent a letter to Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari(أبوموسى ألأشعري), He said: Put fear in the hearts of the evil doers,

the Fussaaq(فساق) the burglars, the Raiders, the gangs, strike fear in their hearts.

Make them think twice before they commit any crime.

By applying the Hudood(حدود) of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ, that's how they establish security for the people.

Number three, Al-Jihad(جهاد) Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله).

It was the responsibility of the Wullaa(ولأء) to establish this great Shaeera(شعيره) of Islam Al-Jihad(جهاد) Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله)

and their roles involved Irsaal Al-Mutatawieen(إرسال ألمتتوعين), sending the volunteers they would organize recruitment in the Masajid(مساجد),

they would be recruited in the Masajid(مساجد).

The Imam(اِمَام) would stand up and recruit them and then all of these recruits would go in and join in the camps and it is the responsibility of the Waalii(والي)

to send them, where they are needed.

Number 2, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) has promised his people, he Said; I promise you, to protect your borders.

So, that was the responsibility of the Wullaa(وُلأء) on the frontier lands to protect the borders from any attacks by the Kuffar(كفار).

Number three Al-Tahseen(ألتّحسين) the building of fortresses, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) told Amr Bin Al-Aas(عَمْرُو بِن اَلْعَاص) to build fortresses in Al-Jesa(ألجيزة)

because in Egypt, it was on the Mediterranean Sea.

So, it could be attacked by the Roman ships.

So, he wanted them to build fortresses.

Number 4. Intelligence it was the responsibility of the Wullaa(وُلأء) to gather intelligence information for the Khalifah(خليفة).

We know that Abu Obaidah(ابوعبيدة) for example, He had many of the Muslims working in gathering intelligence for him, and then he would send that information to Umar Bin Khattab  رضي الله عنه.

Number five. He also Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) asked the Wullaa(ولأء) to raise horses.

So, they would have these pasture lands and they would raise in them hundreds of horses and these horses are for nothing but Al-Jihad(جهاد) Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله),

they would not be used for anything else.

So, for example you had in Al-Basra(ألبصره) actually I did read the numbers.

I just didn't bring them with me.

The number of horses in Al-Basra(ألبصره) and Al-Kufa(ألكوفه) and these were devoted for that cause and it was the responsibility of the Waali(والي)

and he would appoint some men full time to take care of these ranchers.

Number six: The training of the youth Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) ordered that training camps would be opened in every Wulaaya(ولاية).

To train the young, in target shooting, in swimming and in horseback riding in these three areas and even though there was a safety hazard and a report came to Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) that one of these young men died,

in training that did not change a thing.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said; That it should still carry on, even though somebody died.

The training should still go on because this is Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله).

They would be responsible for the financing of the armies and the paying of the salaries to the soldiers and they would also be involved in the negotiation and agreement with the enemies,

so that was number three Number four, They will try their best to provide sustenance for the people, Ar-Rizq(رزق).

Al-Bayhaqi(ألبيهقي) narrates; Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) carried on providing for the Bedouins in the refugee camps, we talked about them.

The Bedouins in the refugee camps that came to Madina.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) carried on spending on them until Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ, elevated the famine of Aam-Er-Ramadah(عام ألرمادة) and rain started falling down

and that is when they started going back to their lands.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب), Al-Bayhaqi(ألبيهقي) said; Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) went on his horse to witness the refugees, when they were leaving Madina and going back to their homes

and it was said that tears started rolling down the cheeks of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب).

So, one man from Muharib(محارب) said; the famine of Ar-Ramada(ألرمادة) was elevated because of you.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said; Woe to you, you can say that if I spent from my own pocket or from the money of Al-Khattab(ألخطاب) from my father

but I was spending from the money of Allah.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) was very emotional when he saw these refugees, bringing their children and their women and they were all going on their camels and leaving the refugee camps.

Where they stayed there for months and months and months, suffering hunger.

many of them died.

And it was Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) as we talked earlier, he would cook for them, serve them, help them and now Al-Hamdolillah(ألحمدلله) the problem was over and they're going back to their territories.

Bilal رضي الله عنه was one of the zuhaad(زهاد) and Bilal(بلال) was very concerned with See! Some people they are austere in themselves, some people they want to be austere

and they want everybody else to be austere.

Bilal(بلال) was one of those people.

Bilal(بلال) was very worried that the Muslim Ummah(امة) would become soft and luxurious.

So, he comes to Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) to complain about what's happening in Syria.

He came to Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) and he said; O Ameer Ul-Mo'mineen(أميرالمؤمنين), your military generals in Ash-Sham(ألشام) are eating the flesh of birds, chicken and different fowl and they are eating soft bread.

While that is not accessible to the rest of the Muslims.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: Bring them, call them.

So, they came to Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) and he said; Is what Bilal(بلال) is claiming is that true.?

Yazeed Bin Abi Sufiyaan(يزيدبن أبي سفيان) said; O Ameer Ul-Mo'mineen(أميرالمؤمنين), what Bilal(بلال) is saying about the food that we eat is true.

But that is because it is very cheap in our land.

And it costs the same as it would cost to feed our families in Al-Hijaz(ألحجاز).

We are spending the same amount of money, we would be spending, if we are in Madina, we are buying these items because in this land, they're very cheap.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: Not until I make sure that you provide for your people.

So, he brought the people and he said: What would be enough food for you in a month.

So, they said: So and So bread and So and So vinegar and So and So olive oil.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said; We write an agreement between you and your Governor's, that they will provide you with that amount of food.

In addition to the handouts that the government gives.

And if they do not fulfill that, you come and raise your complaints to me, and I will make sure that they will give you, what is due to you?

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) did not allow his governors to eat soft bread.

Until he made sure that everyone in Ash-Sham(ألشام) is going with a full stomach everyone has enough for them.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) wanted the governor's to seek Shuraa(شورى) from the seniors and the experienced.

He heard that Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari(أبوموسى ألأشعرى) has an open door policy, when it comes to Shuraa(شورى) anybody can come in and attend the Shuraa(شورى).

The young, the old, the educated, the illiterate everyone.

So, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) told him; He said: Open your doors first to the leaders of the people and to the knowledgeable people,

the people who are knowledgeable in Qur'an, and Islam.

Let them come in first and take their seats.

And then if there any other seats vacant, allow the rest to come in.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) is saying that when it comes to Shura(شورى), you should seek Shuraa(شورى), consultation with the leaders, with the scholars,

with the people of experience, they should come in first, don't just open the doors and have everybody come into your Shuraa(شورى).

And, you know, not only in Shuraa(شورى) is that the case but also in choosing leaders, electing leaders, it applies both to Shuraa(شورى) and the electing of leaders.

It needs to be done by the people of experience and knowledge.

And he told Abu Musa(ابوموسى); He said: People have leaders who represent them in asking for their needs so honor these people.

In the tribal societies the tribe would have leaders and these leaders would go to the Sultan(سلطان) and ask help for his people.

So, and so needs this, so and so needs that… Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) is saying: Honor these people who are helping others.

The governors of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) used to be very caring, not only would they apply justice.

You know?. You could apply justice in a very dry way and stay away from people.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) wanted them to show compassion, - not to show… To feel compassion.

It's not a show to feel compassion and to be caring about the subjects just like a shepherd would care about his flock.

So, when he would meet with the followers with the people he would ask them, How is your Waali(والي)?

They would say he's an excellent man! May Allah reward him.

He would say; Does he visit your ill?

Does he visit the slave?

How does he deal with the weak?

Does he sit on the doorstep of the layman?

If they answer no, to any of these questions.

He would fire him.

He needs to visit the ill and he needs to visit the slaves and he needs to be kind with the weak.

So, it goes beyond being just.

You could be just without visiting the weak.

But he wants them to care about their subjects and to be close to them.

The governors of Umar(عُمَر) would ensure that people are treated equally.

Once Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) was told: That one of his governors gave government handouts this money that the government would give to the subjects,

he gave it to the Arabs and he didn't give it to the non Arabs.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) summoned him and he said; Why haven't you treated the people equally?

People need to be treated equally the days of nationalism and tribalism are over.

And Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) would follow up with his Wulaa(ولاء).

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said; I would rather change the governor every day, then have a governor stay and oppress the people for one hour.

Even if I would have to change him on a daily basis and cause all of that fluctuation and instability is better than having a Wali(والي), who is oppressing the people for even one hour.

He used to say: If I appoint a governor and then that Governor wrongs the people and I know about that then I have wronged them myself and he would say;

He asked the people he said: If I appoint on you, somebody who is good, pious and he is the best and I instruct him to rule with justice.

Have I done my part.?

They said: Definitely.

You appointed somebody who is the best and you instructed him to be just, you have done your part.

He said: No! I haven't.

No, I would not have fulfilled my part until I follow up with him.

And I put him under scrutiny to make sure that he is ruling according to what I instructed him.

So, not only should I appoint the good but I need to follow up.

When he would appoint a governor.

He would ask that the people send the delegation to meet with him on a continuous basis, so that he can ask them about the Ummal(عُمَّالْ).

So, he would receive a delegation of 10 from Al-Kufa(ألكوفه) and when the money from Al-Kufa(ألكوفه) would come and this money is the Kharaaj(خراج) and the Jizya(جزيه) and the Zakat(زكواة).

He would instruct that this money needs to be accompanied by 10 representatives of the people.

When he would receive the money who would ask these representatives. He would say: Do you testify that this money was taken in accordance to the laws of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ

and that no Muslim or non Muslim was wronged.

When they would say yes, he would accept the money.

He didn't want, one Dirham(درهم) to be taken unlawfully from a Muslim or non Muslim and he had to make sure that there are Shuhood(شهود), ten witnesses

to ensure that this money was taken in the right way.

He would have Baraid(بريد) a mail, the mail man would gather all of the letters and he would announce his departure date.

And he would gather all of the letters and he would not be allowed to read any of them.

And the mail would be delivered to Ameer Ul-Mo'mineen(أميرالمؤمنين) in Madina.

So, if anyone had a private complain, they could write it down and send it to the Khalifah(خليفه) without even traveling and no one, would have read that mail.

It's not like that the Waali(والي) has a right to peek into those envelopes based on intelligence information that he is complaining against you.

The Privacy was secured, whatever was written is private, only the Khalifah(خليفه) will read it.

He used to take advantage of the Hajj(حَجْ).

Hajj(حَجْ) was a general assembly.

You know? Now Hajj(حَجْ) today is devoid of its role.

In the time of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) Hajj(حَجْ) was a general assembly.

Where he would ask the people about their governors, it was a Shura(شورى) for Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) to meet with his employees.

It was a time to plan for the next year, it was a time to report what is happening in every Muslim state to the Khalifah(خليفه).

It was a time to hold the leaders accountable to the followers.

That was the role of Hajj(حَجْ) in the time of Umar Bin Khattab رضي الله عنه.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) he said; Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: If I live, I am going to travel for a whole year to the different Muslim states.

Because I'm sure that the people have needs and they're unable to deliver the request to me.

Either their leaders are not bringing those demands forth, or they are not able to send them to me.

So, I would go to Ash-Sham(ألشام) and stay two months.

And then I would go to Iraq and stay for two months and then to Al-Kufa(ألكوفه) and I would stay two months and then also to Al-Basra(ألبصرة) and stay two months.

So, he wanted to go around traveling in order to ensure that every Muslim, every citizen of the Islamic Khilafah(خِلَافَه) has his needs fulfilled.

IT SHUDDERS IN PAIN FREELY MY CHASITY, MY MODESTY!

OH MUSLIM, YOU SAW MY INJURY AND THE INJURY OF MY PRIDE
parts.urdu: وَيُفَقِّهُّمْ  فَإِنِّيْ بِرِجَالٍ يُعَلِّمُوْنَھم
parts.arabic:
بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَانِ الرَّحِيْمَ۝

اَلْحَمْدُ لله ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلى سَيِّدِنَا محمد وَعَلَى اَلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ تَسْلِيْمًا كَثِيْراً وَإِنَّمَا رَجُلٌ اَقْوَى مِنْ رَّجُلْ

"رَجُلٌ اَقْوَى مِنْ رَّجُلْ" اَللَّهُمَّ اِنِّيْ أَشْقُوْ عَلَيْكَ ,عَجْزِلْ مُؤْمِنْ, وَجَلَدِالْكَافِرْ "عَجِبْتُ" لَيْسَ يَتَحَسَّرُ أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ إِلا عَلَى سَاعَةٍ مَرَّتْ بِهِمْ لا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِيهَا

اَلْبَصَرْ بِالْعَمَلْ لَيْسَ الْخَبَرْالكَلْ مُعَيْنَا اَحْرَهْ اَيْنَ يَقَعَأ فِيْ قَاتَلَكَ اللهَ مَا أَرَتْ بِذَالِكَ وَجْه’ الله مَنِسْتَعْمَلَ رَجُلً لِمَوَدَّةْ أَوْ قَرَابَهْ لَا يَشْغَلُه’ إِلَّا ذَالِكْ فَقَدْ خَائِنَاللهَ وَرَسُوْلَه’

مَنْ يَطْلُبُ هَذَا لْأَمْرَلَمْ يُعَنْ عَلَيْهََ سَائِرْلَنَا إِنَّ اللهَ هُوَالْمُسَائِرْ أَلَّا يَرْقَبْ بَرْضُوْنًاً وَلَا يَعْكُلْ نَقِيًّا ,

وَلَا يَلْبِسْ رَقِيْقًا , وَلَا يُغْلِقْ بَابَه’ دُوْنَ حَاجَتَ النَّاسْ, يَا أَحْنَفْ قَدْ بَلَوْتُكَا وَ خَبِرْتُكَا فَرَاأَيْتُ أَنَّا عَلى نِيَّتَكَ حَسَنَا

وَأَنَا أَرْجُوْ أَنْ تَكُوْنَ سَرِيْرَتَكَا مِثْلَعَنَا عَلى نِيَّتِكِ وَاِنَّا كُنَّا نَحَدَّثْ أَنَّا مَا يُحْلِقُ هَذَهِ لّْاُمَّهْ كُلَّا مُنَافِقٍ عَلِيْمَ

ثُمَّ قَالْ , يَا أحْنَفْ أَتَدْرِيْ لِمَا تَبَسْتُكْ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا لَا تُدْنُوْ هُمْ,وَقَدْأَقْصَاهُمُ اللهَ

وَلَا تُكْرِمُوْهُمْ وَقَدْ أَهَانَهُمُ اللهَ وَلَا تَأْمَنُوْ هُمْ وَقَدْ خَوَّ نُهُمُ اللهَ كُنْتُ عَبْدًانَصْرَانِيًا لِعُمر, فَقَالَ: أَسْلِمْ حَتَّى نَسْتَعِيْنَ بِكَ عَلَى بَعْضِ أُمُوْرِ الْمُسْلِمِيْنَ

لِأَنَّه’ لَا يَنْبَغِيْ لَنَا أَنْ نَسْتَعِيْنَ عَلَى أَمُوْرِهِمْ بِمَنْ لَيْسَ مِنْهُمْ لَاِ كْرَاهَا فِى الدِّيْنَ متنكب القوس وَنَحْنُ عِبَادَ الله نَمْشِيْ عَلَى الْأَرْضَ،وَ نَجْلِسُ عَلَى الْأَرْضَ،

وَنَأْكُلُ عَلَى الْأَرْضَ، وَنَضَجِّعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضَ وَلَيْسَ ذَالِكَ يَنْقُصُنَا عِنْدِاللهِ شَيْئَا ، بَلْ يُعَظِّمَ اللهُ بِهِ أَجُوْ رَنَا ، وَيَرْفَعْدَرَجَاتِنَا، وَنَتَوَاضَعُ بِذَالِكَ لِرَبِّنَا

تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتَنْزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ لَا حَاجَةْ لِيْ فِيْهَا وَلَكِنْ أَخْرُجْ مُجَاهِدًا ولِلْمُسْلِمِيْنَ مُعَاوِناً

اقامة دين إِنَّ اَهْلَ الشَّامِ قَدْ كَثَرُوْ وَمَلَاْءُ الْمَدَائِنَ وَحْتَاجُ اِلَى مَنْ يُعَلِّمُ هُمُ الْقُرْآنْ تَخْرُجُ ازَّعِيْنَهْ مِنْ أَلْهِيْرَهْ إِلَي مَكَّهْ

اَخيف لفسّاقأ وَلَكُمْ إِلَيَّ أَنْ أَسُدَّ صُغُرَكُمْ أَنَّا عمر أَنْفَقَا عَلَى أَهْلِ ارَّمَادَهْ حَتَّي وَقَعَ ألْمَتَرْ وَيْحَكْ ذَالِكَ لَوْ أَنْفَقْتَ مِنْ مَّالِيْ أَوْ مِنْ مَّالِ الْخَطَّابْ إِنَّمَا أَنْفَقْتُ مِّنْ مَّالِ الله

يَا أمير المؤمنين إِنَّ أُلمَّرَآ أَجْنَادَكَ بِشَّامِ وَاللهِ مَا يَاكُلُوْنَا إِلَّا هُمُّ طَّيْرَ وَخَبْزًا نَقِيْ وَمَا يِجِدُوْ ذَالِكَ عَامَّةِ الْمُسْلِمِيْنَ

بَلَغَنِيْ أَنَّكَ تَعْزَنُ الِّنَّاسِ جَمًّا غَفِيْراً فَإِذَاجَآءَكَ كِتَابِ هَذَا فَعْزَنْ لِأَهْلِ الشَّرَفِيْ وَأَهْلِ الْقُرْآنَ وَتَّقْوَى وَدِّيْنَ

فَإِذَا أَخَذُوْ مَجَالِسَ هُمْ فَعْزَنْ لِلْعَامَّهْ لَمْ يَزَلِلنَّاسِ وُجُوْهُ يَرْفَعُوْنَ هَوَاءِجَالنَّاسِ فَأَكْرِمُوْ وَجُوْهَالنَّاسْ

هَلْ يَعُوْضُوْ مَرْضَاكُمْ؟

هَلْ يَعُوْضُوْ الْعَبْدَ؟

كَيْفَ صَنْعِيَ أَوْ بِضَعِيُفَ؟

هَلْ يَجْلِسُ عَلَى بَابْ؟

خَيْرُ الِّيْ أَنْ أَعْزِلَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ وَآلِيًا مِنْ أَنْ أُبْقِيْ ظَالِمًا سَاعَتْ أَنْهَارْ أَيُّ مِنْ عَامِ الِّيْ ظَلَمَ اَحَدًا فَبَلَغَنِيْ مَظْلَمَتَا فَلَمْ أُغَيَّرَهَا فَأَنْ أَظْلَمْتَا

أَرَأَيْتُ مِنَّ اسْتَعْمَلْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ خَيْرُ مَنْ اَعْلَمْ ثُمَّ أَمَرْتُه’ بِلْ عَدْلِ أَكُنْتُ قَضَيْتُمَا عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُ نَعْمَ قَالَ لَا، حَتَّى أَنْظُرَفِيْ عَمَلِيْهِ أَعَمِلَ بِمَا أَمَرْتَه’ عَمْلَا

لَإِنْ إِشْتُ إِنْ شَاءَاللهُ لَا أَسِيْرَنَّا فِى رَّعِيَّتِ حَوْلَا فَإِنِّيْ أَعْلَمُوْأَنَّا لِا لنَّاسِ حَوَائِجْ تُكْتَ عَدُوْنِيْ إِمَّا عُمَّالَهُمْ فَلَا إِدْفَعُوْنَ اِلَيْهِ فَإِمَّالَهُمْ لَايَسِلُوْنَ اِلَيْهِ

فَا أَسِيْرَ إِلَّى الشَّامْ فَأُقِيْمَ بِهَا شَهْرَيْنَ ثُمَّ أَسِيْرُ إِلَى الْجَزِيْرَهْ فَأُقِيْمُ بِهَا شَهْرَيْنَ

parts.english:
Tonight we'll talk about the famous, nightly patrols of the Ameer Ul Mo'mineen(أمير المؤمنين) Umar Bin Khattab رضي الله عنه.

These are some of the most amazing stories of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب).

The Khalifah(خليفه) going around at night on patrols, to make sure that his Ummah(امة) is fine and well, to make sure that they are happy, to make sure that they are content.

And he would take along with him people like Abdur Rahman Ibn Auf رضى الله عنه.

He would take with him, his servant Salim(سالم), he would take with him his servant Yarfah(يرفه).

He had different people accompany him on these journeys.

One night Umar Bin Khattab رضي الله عنه, saw some guests in the Masjid(مسجد).

These were travelers and the travelers would sometimes stay at Al-Masjid-Al-Nabwi(ألمسجد ألنبوي) they would sleep on Al-Musallah(مصله).

The Masjid(مسجد) was open there's no lock pad.

What are you going to steal from "Masjid-Al-Nabwi(مسجد ألنبوي)" no speakers, no microphones, no rugs, so it's open.

These travelers Abiree Sabeel(عا برى سبيل) would spend their night in the Musallah(مصله).

Umar Bin Khattab رضي الله عنه told Abdur Rahman Ibn Auf(عبدالرحمن إبن عوف), would you like to join me, so we could guard them this evening.

Now, they have belongings, so Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) wanted to guard them.

And what can you say about such a thing?

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) guarding these travelers.

You can say it's humbleness, you can say it's a sense of responsibility, you can say it's love for Muslims, you call it whatever you want.

So, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) is telling another man who was among the10 who were given the glad tidings of Jannah(جنة) You know Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) and Abdur Rahman Ibn Auf(عبدالرحمن إبن عوف) and their likes,

they've already been given the Bushra Bil-Jannah(بشرا بالجنة).

They are among the 10 who are given the glad tidings of Jannah(جنة), so why not just sit at home.

Why do you have to go through all of this hassle and difficulty, you already have that badge of honor.

Just do your Salah(صلاة) do your Ibadaat(عبادات) and that's enough, you're Khalifah(خليفه) and you're guarding and you're spending the hours of the night

these people are sleeping and you're guarding them.

Abdur Rahman bin Auf (عبدالرحمن إبن عوف) said: Yes! Definitely.

So, Umar Bin Khattab رضي الله عنه, he hears a child crying, an infant was crying.

He is crying for some time, so Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) goes to the mother and says, Fear Allah and take care of your child and then he leaves.

The child is carry on crying, he is crying again, He is crying again.

Towards the end of the night, he goes to her and say, what kind of mother are you?

You are an evil mother, your child has been crying since the beginning of the night.

She said: I'm trying to wean him, but he doesn't want to eat the food.

This child still wants to breastfeed and his mother is trying to convince him to eat, rather than breastfeed.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: Why are you trying to wean him, how old is he?

She said: He's a few months old.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said; Why are you trying to wean him then?

Because the complete period of breastfeeding is how long! Two years, so he said: Why are you trying to wean him.?

She said: "Because Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) does not start paying them, until they are weaned." Ameer Ul-Mo'mineen(أميرالمؤمنين) does not give the handouts

except when the child reaches Al-Fitaar(ألفطار).

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: Woe to you, son of Al-Khattab(الخطاب), What have you done?

And he then in Salat-Ul-Fajar(صلاة الفجر) he was so taken back by what happened people could not recognize his Qira'ah(قراءة) because of his crying,

he was weeping so bad they couldn’t recognize his recitation.

And then he immediately after Salat-Ul-Fajar(صلاة الفجر) issues an order, a government order to the mothers around the Muslim world, he sent this message all over, he said;

Don't wean your children too early, because from now on, you will receive a handout the day your child is born.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: How many children have I killed?

How many children have been killed because of you?

What is Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) saying, who did he killed?

Which children did he kill?

This is a favor that he's doing to the people, he's giving them these handouts.

But he was so emotional because of what he saw, and he was so upset with the law that state that they should be given this money at the age of two.

He considered that he has harmed the Muslim infants because their mothers are trying to wean them sooner to get the handouts.

Can you think about such a government you don't pay any taxes and you still receive handouts from the government.

Ya'ani(يعني) now governments are ripping their people off, taking 30% in taxes or more and they give you nothing.

Supposedly they take this money to offer you services.

Where does all of that money go?

So much money, Where does it go?

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab( عمر ابن الخطاب), first of all, in the Islamic Khilafah(خِلَافَه), there was nothing called the Zariba(ضريبة) no taxes at all.

They didn't know the concept of taxes.

This concept of Al-Makoos(المكوس), was something that existed among the Romans and the Persians.

In Khilafah(خِلَافَه) Al-Islamia no Al-Makoos(المكوس).

All what would be taken from you is Zakat(زكواة) if you are capable of giving it and Ushur(أشور), this is something that was started by Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) and that's like customs

for businessmen who are coming from outside Al-Khilafah(خِلَافَه), they would pay customs, and we'll talk about that later on.

But the government gives you money and the moment your child is born you're gonna start receiving those handouts.

During one of his patrols, he passes by this house and you know in those days the house didn't have a front yard in the backyard, and a huge garden and soundproof walls,

these were very modest buildings, mud bricks and the house is basically composed of a few rooms and that's it, not very high.

The house of Rasool Allah ﷺ one could touch the ceiling with your hand as Al-Hasan Al-Basri(الحسن البصرى) said.

So, you could hear what's happening inside these houses.

So Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) is walking and he hears a woman and this was very late at night.

This woman was reciting lines of poetry.

The lines go on and in the end , she says, Basically, this woman was a wife of one of the Mujahideen(مجاهدين) Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله)

her husband was away for a very long time and she was feeling very lonely.

She has no children, she staying at home alone.

So, she was reciting these lines of poetry.

The first line, what it means is, this night is very, very long, and I have no companion to be with me.

And then she goes on to say that if it wasn't for Allahعَزّوجَلّ, I would have been with another man, so basically, she's saying, if it wasn't for Allah, I would have committed Haram(حرام).

And then she said, but because I fear Allahعَزّوجَلّ and because there's an eye that is watching me all the time.

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ has appointed two angels to you, one on the right and one on the left.

She said: If it wasn't for that I would have, had the companion with me now.

Umar Bin Khattab رضي الله عنه  said; May Allahعَزّوجَلّ have mercy on you.

He wasn't speaking to her he was making the Dua(دُعَا) for her and then he goes to his daughter Hafsah(حفصه), Umm Ul-Mo'mineen(أم المؤمنين),

and he knocks and Hafsah(حفصه) said: Oh my father, Why did you come in this late hour, it must be something very urgent.

So, he comes in and he says: For how long can a woman wait for her husband?

How long can she stay alone?

How long will her patience last?

So Hafsah(حفصه) said: One month, two months, three months, and then after four months her patience runs out.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) immediately issues his orders that no Muslim soldier should stay away from his wife more than four months.

So, the rotation is four months you know, even today with the fast modes of transportation, they don't do four months services, six months a year.

But Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: If that's how long she can wait.

We don't want our sisters to wait longer than that, if four months is the limit then they should come back after four months.

But there was a problem, many of those soldiers didn't want to come back.

You know, now soldiers are crying, we want to go back to mom and dad.

I want to go back to my girlfriend.

They are weeping they are crying, you see them on TV, they're crying all the time.

But these who were Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله) some of them didn't want to go back.

So, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) had to force them, he sent some orders.

He said: You either go back or I'm going to give you an exemption but you have to give Nafaqa(نفقه) to your wife, sufficient money you have to provide her with sufficient money, so that she wouldn't be in any need,

otherwise you divorce.

Otherwise you divorce.

So, you see that these are teachings that show the care that Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) had for the Muslim family.

How eager he was to make sure that men are happy, women are happy, children are happy.

So, four months was the maximum time but what happened was, in the time of Umar(عُمَر) because now the land that was conquered was expanding

and it was getting further away from Makkah and Madina.

They were starting to establish towns up north and these were military towns like Al-Basra(ألبصرة), Al-Kufa(الكوفه), Al-Mosul(الموصل), Al-Fustat(ألفستات), Al-Jeza(ألجيزة).

All of  these were towns that were founded my Muslims.

Baghdad(بغداد) was later on founded by Al-Abbasieen(ألعباسيين).

So, you can see that the most important towns in Iraq were actually founded in the time of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) Al-Kufa(الكوفه), Al-Basra(ألبصرة), Al-Mosul(الموصل), these are some of the most famous towns in Iraq.

These were initially military towns.

To make it easy on the soldiers, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب), he has sent orders to his commanders to build new towns, so that the Muslims can bring their families in, and they set base there.

Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله) these towns became, so important and so vibrant that the weight of the Muslim world was actually in those towns

and they became more important commercially and politically, then Makkah Madina.

Obviously Makkah and Madina retain their religious importance but politically and commercially these other towns picked up.

So, you see that in the time of Ali Ibn Abi Talib(علي ابن ابي طالب) he actually moved the capital of Khilafah(خِلَافَه) from Al-Madina to Al-Kufa(ألكوفه).

They were becoming the center of the Muslim world and then Damascus, and Jerusalem and Al-Fustat(ألفستات) which grew later to become a Cairo.

But it was because of Al-Ghazoo(ألغزؤ) because of these military expeditions that these towns were founded and that's what gave them prominence and importance.

So, now they were moving with their families and going up north to these lands of Ribat(رباط).

So, you can see that how the Ghazoo(غزؤ) was really the central theme with the Khulafah رضي الله عنهم and you would find that everything revolves around it even commerce, business, building towns everything.

In another occasion, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) heard this woman also apparently a wife of one of the soldiers, who was absent it was one line poetry. She said:

Is there any way for me to get hold of a cup of wine to drink, and is there any way of me to get in touch with Nasr Bin Hajjaj(نصر بن حجاج).

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) did not like these words.

So, next day in the morning he asks for Nasr Bin Hajjaj(نصر بن حجاج).

Who is this man Nasr Bin Hajjaj(نصر بن حجاج)?

So they brought him in and it turns out that Nasr Bin Hajjaj(نصر بن حجاج) was a young man in Madina and he was a very handsome young man, and this woman was asking for wine and asking for Nasr Bin Hajjaj(نصر بن حجاج).

Now Nasr Bin Hajjaj(نصر بن حجاج) had some fancy hair.

So, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) said: Shave his head.

They shaved his head, apparently didn't really change him much he even became more handsome.

So, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: Put Imamah(إمامة) on, he became more handsome.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: Exiled him out of Madina! Exiled him out of Madina.

You might be wondering, it's not the fault of Nasr Bin Hajjaj(نصر بن حجاج) why send him out of Madina.?

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) was very strict in his commands, he said get him out of Madina and I don't want him here causing me problems.

Women singing songs about Nasr Bin Hajjaj(نصر بن حجاج), get him out.

So, they sent them to Al-Basra(ألبصرة).

The reason, why he sent him to Al-Basra(ألبصرة), you might say well he's going to cause Fitnah(فِتْنَه) in Al-Basra(ألبصرة).

The reason why he sent him to Al-Basra(ألبصرة) is because Al-Basra(ألبصرة) is a military town.

He is going to be around soldiers.

However, in Madina, it's peaceful, Madina wasn't in a state of war, During the time of Umar(عمر), Uthman(عثمان), it was peaceful.

and in that environment Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) did not want to have any Fitnah(فِتْنَه) going on.

So, he sends him to this military town rather than have him, fixing the style of his hair in Madina, have him go up north and fight.

So, he sends him to Al-Basra(ألبصرة) when the woman heard about that she was very afraid that Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) might hold her accountable for what she said so.

So, she sent him some lines of poetry saying that, I didn't really mean that literally, it was figurative speech, and I have Taqwa(تقوى) of Allahعَزّوجَلّ and I fear Allahعَزّوجَلّ

and I'm not going to get involved in any of that Haram(حرام).

Now, this was just poetry that I was reciting.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: Al-hamdolillah(ألحمدلله), that Allahعَزّوجَلّ has tamed your desires with Taqwa(تقوى) of Allah.

Al-hamdolilllah(ألحمدلله) that Allah has tamed the desires with Taqwa(تقوى).

People have these desires men and women but the piety the righteousness in your heart tames those desires.

So, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) was happy when he heard that.

Nasr Bin Hajjaj(نصر بن حجاج) sent him a letter saying that he wants to come back to Madina.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: Not when I'm alive, not as long as I'm alive, you're not coming into Madina and he only came back after Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) passed away.

So, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) again he wasn't sentimental he wasn't emotional he was very strict when it came to the rules, he wanted to make sure that the benefit of the whole is preserved

maybe Nasr Bin Hajjaj(نصر بن حجاج) is not at fault, this woman he accepted her explanation, however Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) does not want to have Fitnah(فِتْنَه) around.

During another night excursion of Ameer Ul Mo'mineen رضي الله عنه keep in mind that he was the greatest king of his time, greatest leader of his time

we shouldn't say King because he wouldn't approve of that title for himself.

Even though, he had a greater status than the kings of the world.

He was with his servant Yarfaa(يرفع) or Salim(سالم), one of them and he saw in the distance one woman with her children and she had a camp fire.

So, this is a woman alone with her children.

So, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) sees that fire he wants to check it out, he goes there and when it gets close to the fire and he sees who was around the fire, it was very cold night.

He said; Peace be upon you. People of the light.

She responded, she said: Alaikum-Us-Salaam(عليكم السلام), He said: Adinoo(أأدنو), Can I come near?

She said: You come near for good, otherwise stay away.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب), he approached her and she was surrounded with her little ones and they were crying.

He said: "What's the problem?" She said: "We are here because of the cold weather and hunger." They were traveling and they couldn't go any further.

They were so hungry and tired, they set camp in that area.

And the children were very hungry.

So, they were crying constantly.

And Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: So what is this?

She said: This is water that is boiling, I'm trying to keep the kids preoccupied with it." What she did was, she was boiling rocks in water, rocks, stones,

she was dropped them in that port and she was boiling it.

So, that she could tell the kids that food is coming, until they become tired and sleep.

She just wants them to get off crying because they were crying constantly.

So, she said, All right. Don't worry. Food is coming.

And she's boiling for them rocks with the hope that eventually they'll get tired and fall asleep.

What did she say?

She said: We are cold and we are so hungry and Allahعَزّوجَلّ will be the judge between us and Umar(عُمَر).

She said: "Allah will be the judge between us and Umar(عُمَر)." Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب), She doesn't know she's speaking to Umar(عُمَر).

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said: May Allah have mercy on you and how does Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) know your condition?" She said: What do you mean, how does he know our condition.?

"How can he assume responsibility over our affairs and then neglect us?" He is our leader, he is responsible for our affairs, so how can he neglect us, he should know.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب), he immediately stood up and he went with his servant, his servant said; We were running, Aslam(أسلم) said: And we were just running,

he said; We went to the storage, where they used to store the flour, so we grabbed a sack of flour and some animal shortening, fat and he told his servant carry it on my back, carry it over my shoulders,

Aslam(أسلم) said; "Ameer Ul Momineen(أميرالمؤمنين) I'm going to carry it for you.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said; Woe to you, are you gonna carry for me my sins on the Day of Judgment, carry it on my back, so he puts it on the back of Ameer Ul Mo'mineen(أميرالمؤمنين).

And Ameer ul Mo'mineen(أميرالمؤمنين) goes to that woman and he's cooking for her.

Ameer Ul Mo'mineen(أميرالمؤمنين) Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) is cooking for this women.

He didn't give it to her and tell her you cook, he was cooking.

Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله) the servant Aslam(أسلم) said; I saw Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) bending under the pot to blow into the fire,

to ignite it and I was seeing smoke going through his beard.

Imagine the Ameer Ul Mo'mineen(أميرالمؤمنين) going under and blowing the fire and all of the smoke is coming in his face and going through his beard,

until he cooked the food and then he served it himself to the children.

And then he went a side, so his servant came to him and said: Do you have anything else to do.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) did not respond back.

Aslam(أسلم) said: We remained there until the kids were knocked out, that's it they all fell asleep.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) said; I didn't want to leave until, I made sure that they're all asleep and happy, and then they went back.

Before he left, this woman told Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب).

She said: "You deserve to be the Khalifah(خليفه) more than Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب)" you should be the Khalifah(خليفه), not him.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) told her: Don't say but good.

He doesn’t want to make Gheebah(غيبة) about the Khalifah(خليفه).

He said: Don’t speak except good, don’t say anything but good.

And if you happen to visit the Khalifah(خليفه), one day you will find me there, you'll find me there and he left.

He didn't tell her that I'm Ameer Ul Mo'mineen(أميرالمؤمنين), he just left.

She was very happy and she was making Dua(دُعَا) for him, she doesn't know that she's making Dua(دُعَا) for Ameer ul Mo'mineen(أميرالمؤمنين) Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب),

whom she was complaining about.

Now, how would Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) know the condition of everyone and how can you hold Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) accountable for every child that is hungry when he's doing his best.

But Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله), the Muslims in those days were used to being, so pampered by the Khulafa(خلفاء), that it was something that they expected, at least this woman did.

When in reality it's not Umar(عُمَر) who's responsible for the fate of every single person when he's doing his best to help them and serve them.

Allahعَزّوجَلّ does not overburden a soul, with something that he cannot carry.

During one of his patrols he saw a wool tent, it wasn't there before this the first time he saw the tent so he said: Let's go and check that tent out.

So he goes there and he finds a man sitting out of the tent and there was a woman in the tent and she was moaning in pain.
