when Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) said: We have more rights to Rasool Allah ﷺ then you.

Because we made Hijrah(هجرة) before you.

Asma Bint Umais(اسماء بنت عميس), she just arrived from Abyssinia.

Asma Bint Umais(اسماء بنت عميس) responded by saying; No, that's not true.

You were with Rasool Allah ﷺ, He was feeding the hungry among you, And was teaching the ignorant among you.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ was the father of this Ummah(امة), and that is how, his marriage life, even is a reflection of that.

An important event occurred during the Prophet Hood of Muhammadﷺ.

A flood has affected the structure of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) is located in a low valley between mountains.

And Makkah was once flooded.

And the flood has caused cracks in the walls of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

So, the people of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) felt the need to rebuild Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) again.

Now Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) in total has been built and rebuilt five or four times, depending on, who was the first to build it.

There's a difference of opinion on whether Ibrahim عليه السّلام was the first to build Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

Some scholars refer to our father Adam عليه السّلام as the first one to build Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

However, the majority opinion is that it was Ibrahim عليه السّلام, who first built it.

Now, the ones who say that Adam عليه السّلام is the one, who built it, they say will not contradicting Qur'an, because Qur'an says; They say that Qur'an states that Ibrahim(اِبْراهِيْم) was raising the foundations of the house.

Meaning there was already something there for him to raise above it.

So, they say that the house, the foundations of it, were established in the time of Adam عليه السّلام.

But the common belief among our scholars is that it was Ibrahim عليه السّلام, who first built it.

However, there is no dispute in the holiness of the place, since the earth was created.

I mean, all of our scholars say even if it wasn't Adam(آدم), who first built it, the place was sacred, was holy, and was visited by the Prophets of Allah.

So, they say it used to be like a small hill, which was destined as a sacred and holy place.

And the Ambiyaa(أنبِيَاء) of Allah would visit it.

And we have references of quite a few Ambiyaa(أنبِيَاء), visiting the house of Allah.

There's a Hadith(حديث) that states that Hood(هود) visited Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), there's a Hadith(حديث) that says that Salih(صالح) visited, Noah(نوح)

and there's a saying attributed to Rasool Allah ﷺ that Eesa عليه السّلام when he comes down again, when he descends to earth in a second coming, he will make Hajj(حج).

So, it's either Adam(آدم) or Ibrahim عليه السّلام who first built Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), but we all know that, it was the first house built for the remembrance of Allah.

First house established for My worship was the one in Bakkah(بكة), Bakkah(بكة) is also another name for Makkah.

So, you have Adam(آدم) and Ibrahim(اِبْراهِيْم).

Let's start counting from Ibrahim عليه السّلام, so Ibrahim عليه السّلام is the first.

Second time was this time we're talking about now, when Makkah was flooded.

The people Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) wanted to rebuild it.

They gathered together and they had to tear it down.

But none of them agreed to make that move.

So, they're all waiting ready with their equipment around Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

But no one wants to go ahead and start bringing down that is how much honor and respect they had for Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) in their hearts,

even though at the time they were Mushrikeen(مشركين).

But they feared Allah سبحانه وتعالى and they thought that it's a dangerous thing to tear down the walls of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

And then one of them said: I will be the first to do it, and he gathered all of his sons and they came early in the morning, and they started bringing the rocks of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) down and they were saying;

O Allah, Don't be afraid, all what we want is good.

So, you can see, their also, their false understanding of the divinity of Allah سبحانه وتعالى.

They were trying to calm God, by telling don't be afraid all what we want is good, Allah سبحانه وتعالى knows what's in your hearts, you don't have to tell him that.

So, even though they believed in Allah, but the in terms of the attributes of Allah.

They had some problems with that.

So, they brought down the walls of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

Now it happened that there was a Roman ship that crashed on a port on the Red Sea close to Makkah.

So, they brought some of the wood on that ship.

And there was a Roman builder who was on that ship.

So, they also had him help with the wood.

So, this was the first time they made the roof of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), the ceiling of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) from wood.

They use some of the wood from this ship.

Now the people of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ), they knew that money from interest was no good.

And they made a decision that they're only going to use Halal(حلال) money, in the rebuilding of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

They're not going to use money from interest or money from prostitution, because at that time to show their corruptness.

And by the way, there's a Hadith(حديث) that is narrated by Al-Bukhari(بخاريْ).

Ayesha رضي الله عنها talks about the types of marriages that existed in Arabia.

It's on page 11, you can refer to it later on.

But the prostitution was something that existed, and you would have men hiring their slave girls, as an income generating source for them.

But they knew that this was not good.

They would do it, they would deal with interest.

But they knew that this was not good.

So, they decided that they're not going to use this money in the rebuilding of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

Since they ran short of funds.

They ended up shortening Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), You know Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) originally was a bit of a rectangle rather than a square.

It was rectangular in shape.

Because the people of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) ran short of funds.

They ended up shortening Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) from one side.

So, they made it a square rather than a rectangle to save money.

The area of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), which they left out was, what we refer today as Al-Hijr(ألحجر), the enclosed area in that semi circle, if you ever visited Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه),

you would see that on one side of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), there's a semi circle that used to be part of the original building of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

And Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) also had two gates, they made it one and they raised the doorstep.

So, now in order to get access to the door, you have to climb, the gate was made very high.

Rasool Allah ﷺ says in this Hadith(حديث), don't, you know Rasool Ullah is talking to Ayesha(عائشه), don't you know that your people had insufficient funds for the expenses.

If it were not, for the fact that your people were only recently unbelievers, I would have torn down the Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) and made for it one door on the east and another on the west,

and I would have included the Al-Hijr(الحجر) area within it.

When Rasool Allah ﷺ opened Makkah, he was thinking about reconstructing Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) on the original foundations.

But then he told Ayesha(عائشه), the reason I'm not going to do this.?

Is because your people just became Muslim, their Islam is soft, their Eeman(إيمان) is weak.

And it might be a Fitnah(فِتْنَه) for them, it might cause them a problem, if I reconstruct Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

So he didn't do it.

There's an important lesson to learn from this Hadith(حديث), and that is that the Daiyah(داعيه) needs to take the condition of the people into consideration.

Even though Rasool Allah ﷺ wanted to do this, but he didn't, because he was worried that it might affect the Eeman(إيمان) of the people.

So, as a person who's calling to Islam, you need to take into consideration, the condition of the people that you're directing the message to.

Abdullah Bin Masood(عبد الله بن مسعود) says that if you tell the people something that is beyond their comprehension, or understanding or Eeman(إيمان), it might be a trial for some of them.

It might cause the backlash with some people.

Sometimes we throw out information on a particular subject, which is absolutely true and valid.

But because the people are not ready for it yet, because their Eeman(إيمان) is weak, it causes a backlash with them.

Some things people just are unable to grasp.

Now, Rasool Allah ﷺ said that your people, Quraish(قُرَيْشْ), the reason why they made the door of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) high is because they wanted to have control on who, would go in and out.

It was an issue of power.

They didn't want to make the door low, so that it would be accessible to anyone.

They made it high so that they could control who would go in and out it's a matter of influence, having authority.

So, the door of the Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) was raised.

Rasool Allah ﷺ said: If I would rebuild it, I would lower the gate.

And I would make for it two gates, so that people could come from one side and leave from the other.

Rather than having to come in and out from the same door.

Rasool Allah ﷺ participated in the rebuilding of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

And at the time, he was maybe around 35 years old.

That's a rough estimate.

So, now the people of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) are building Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), they reached to the holiest part of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), which is the Blackstone.

And now disputes erupts among them, who will have the honor to place the Blackstone in its spot.

Because when they were rebuilding Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), every tribe took responsibility of building one side of it, they all want to participate in this honor.

But with the black stone they disputed, every tribe wanted to have the honor of putting it in its place.

Bannu Abdd-ud-Da'ar(بنو عبدالدار) they gathered all of their men, and they came in front of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) with a pot of blood.

And they placed it in front of everyone.

And they all stuck their hands in the blood and pulled it out.

In other words, they're telling everyone that this is what will happen if we don't place the Blackstone in its place.

So, it's like pledging to die and to fight.

We will do it otherwise, this is what will happen, blood will flow.

Even though that was a drastic measure, and quite a threat.

But that wasn't enough to deter others, another tribe they went and bought in their own pot of blood.

And they started sticking their hands in and pulling them out.

And then everybody was bringing their own pots of blood and it was four or five days they couldn't solve the problem and war was about to erupt between them.

And then the eldest man among them, Umayyah(أميه), he had a suggestion.

He came and said: Let's agree that the first man to walk in, towards Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), will be given complete authority in judging between us.

So, they all gather next to Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) and, they were waiting for the first person to come.

And the first person to walk in was Muhammadﷺ they all stood up and said: The truthful and the trustworthy, we all agree.

Now they have already agreed that they will give complete authority to the person who would come in, but they were so happy that, this person was Muhammadﷺ because they knew that he will not be biased in his ruling.

You know, it would be expected that if someone came from a particular family, he would give authority to his family to place it in it's place.

I mean, and that was the expected thing that we're going to leave it randomly for the first one to come in, and his family would take it, but when they saw that it was Muhammadﷺ, they were so happy because they know his fairness.

So, they told him, we give you complete authority in solving this dispute.

Rasool Allah ﷺ asked them to bring a robe, a piece of cloth.

He picked up the black stone and placed it, on this cloth.

And then he asked a representative from each clan to hold the cloth from one side.

And then they all raised it up together, in the same time.

Therefore every one of them will participate in lifting the black stone.

And when they all lifted it up, then heﷺ, with his blessed hands picked up the black stone and placed it in, its place.

So, it was Rasool Allah ﷺ who put the Blackstone in its spot.

So that's the second time Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) was rebuilt.

Rasool Allah ﷺ opened Makkah and then he said that if it wasn't for the fact that the people are new Muslims, I would have rebuilt it on the foundations of Ibrahim(اِبْراهِيْم).

Years later, Abdullah Bin Zubair(عبدالله بن زبير) became the Ameer(امير) of Makkah.

He knew of this Hadith(حديث), because Ayesha(عائشه) was his aunt.

Abdullah Bin Zubair(عبدالله بن زبير), his mother is Asma Bint Abi Bakr(أسماء بنت ابي بكر) the sister of Ayesha(عائشه), so Ayesha(عائشه) was his aunt and he was familiar with this Hadith(حديث).

So, he decided to rebuild Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) on the original foundations because now the people have been Muslim for a long time.

They are not new Muslims anymore, they will be able to handle the situation.

He decided that he's gonna rebuild Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) especially that Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) was burnt because Al-Hajjaj Bin Yousaf Al-Thaqafi(ألحجاج بن يوسف أثقفي), he has laid siege on Makkah.

At that time, there was a war between Abdullah Bin Zubair(عبدالله بن زبير), and Banni Ummayayah(بني أمية) in Syria.

And the Army General of Bannu Umayyah(بنو امية) has laid siege to Makkah.

And one of the catapults has hit Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) and it caused some damage and it burned.

Now that damage could have been fixed without tearing down Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), but Abdullah Bin Zubair(عبد الله بن زبير) wanted to take advantage

and rebuild Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) on the original foundations which he did.

And he fulfilled the description that was given by Rasool Allah ﷺ in the Hadith(حديث), that he would lower the gate and have an East door and a Western door

and expand the size of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) towards Al-Hijr(الحجر), which he did.

So, that's the third time Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) was rebuilt, Abdullah Bin Zubair(عبدالله بن زبير) ended up losing the war and he was killed,

Al-Hajjaj Bin Yousuf(الحجاج بن يوسف) took over.

The Khalifah(خليفه) of that time Abdul-Malik Bin Marwaan(عبدالملك بن مروان) was not familiar with this Hadith(حديث).

So, he gave his commands to take back Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) to the way it was before Abdullah Bin Zubair(عبدالله بن زبير).

So, Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) was shortened again, according to the way that people of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) built it.

After the Khilafah(خلافة) of Bannu Umayyah(بنو امية), Bannu Abbas(بنوعباس) were the family of Khulafah(خلافاء).

One of the Khulafah(خلافاء) of Bannu Abbas(بنوعباس) was thinking about rebuilding Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) again, on the original foundations, and he consulted Al-Imam Malik(الامام مالك),

Imam Malik(امام مالك) told the Khalifah(خليفه) and he gave him a very wise answer.

He said: We don't want Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) to be a toy in the hands of kings.

They keep changing its size every now and then, even though the plan of Rasool Allah ﷺ and his desire was to build it on the foundations of Ibrahim(اِبْراهِيْم),

but let's keep it the way it is and not change it anymore.

Because it was going back and forth on the foundations of Ibrahim(اِبْراهِيْم) and then the way Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) built it and then again on the foundations of Ibrahim(اِبْراهِيْم).

Imam Malik(امام مالك) said that, the people have known Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) and they have known these stones the way they are, don't keep on changing it, keep it the way it is.

And that was a very wise advice from Al-Imam Malik(الامام مالك) which the Khalifah(خليفه) followed.

So, the Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) that we have today is built on which foundation, the foundation of Ibrahim(اِبْراهِيْم) or the foundations of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ)?

But Al-Hamdolillah(الحمدلله) that's something good.

Why.?

If Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) was built on the original foundations of Ibrahim(اِبْراهِيْم), we would have been deprived the chance of praying inside Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

But since it is shortened.

That area which is enclosedby the semi circle is actually part of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

So, when you pray in that area, it is as if you have prayed inside Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

And we know that Rasool Allah ﷺ did pray inside Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

When he opened Makkah, he prayed inside Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), he prayed eight Rak'ah(ركعة) inside Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

So, now we have a chance to pray in Al-Hijr(الحجر).

Otherwise, we would have to get permission to get inside Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) and it would be very cumbersome and difficult.

But now we can pray inside Al-Hijr(الحجر) and it will count as if you prayed in Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

Now over the time, the height of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) has increased, but the size of it has remained constant.

Now, with the stones that Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), are built from, many of them are remnants of the original stones that were used by Ibrahim عليه السّلام,

but not all of them. Some other ones were introduced later by Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) and others.

But the black stone is the original stone that was used by Ibrahim عليه السّلام.

The black stone has never changed, it is the original stone that was given to Ibrahim عليه السّلام.

And there are many stories about the black stone itself.

Some say it originated from Jannah(جنة), there's a Hadith(حديث) that is authentic that says that the black stone was white, but then it turned black because of the sins of the sons of Adam(آدم).

And there is a Hadith(حديث) that says that the black stone is right hand of Allah on Earth.

So, the black stone is very special, it's very honored, and it's very respected and it's the only part of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) that is kissed

and is only part of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) that is pointed to from a distance.

Some people they point to the Yemeni corner which is wrong and Yemeni corner you can touch it when you're passing by it.

But one should not point towards it, or greet it from a distance that is only for the black stone.

So, this is the history of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

The Prophet ﷺ would go out of Makkah and spend time in the cave of Hira(حرا) in a mountain that is fairly close to Makkah a few kilometers away from Makkah.

Rasool Allah ﷺ will take with him provisions, some food and he would go and stay in seclusion, solitude in this cave, worshiping Allah سبحانه وتعالى,

and from the cave it is said that you are able to see Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), in those old days.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ would spend days and nights continuously in the cave, worshipping Allah سبحانه وتعالى before Prophet hood.

So, he knew Allah سبحانه وتعالى and he was worshipping Allah سبحانه وتعالى in that cave.

And this was a chance for Rasool Allah ﷺ to do reflectionand contemplation in the creation of Allah.

And this was training for him Allahسبحانه وتعالى was training him through these moments of reflection and contemplation, because they purify the heart.

And Saeed Hawwa(سعيد هوّا), he comments on this, he says: Solitude was the tradition of some, who seek the guidance of Allah, with the remembrance of Allah and worship.

It was used to illuminate the hearts and remove its Shadows by disconnecting it from its heedlessness and desires.

Some would advise this in the beginning of the journey to belief, as this was the example of the Prophet ﷺ, when he spent time in solitude before and at the beginning of his apostleship.

So, as a Muslim, you are recommended to spend time alone in Zikr(زكر), for example, early in the morning, after Asr(عصر), between Asr(عصر) and Maghrib(مغرب) on Friday.

So, you spend time alone remembering Allah in solitude.

And our scholars talked about the benefit of solitude.

Now, one should not go into the extremes of leaving the society completely, or immersing oneself in the society completely, it should have a middle road.

So, you spend some time with people socializing, but you also spend time alone between you and Allah.

Qiyaam Ul Lail(قيام اليل) is a chance for solitude, praying at night alone when everybody's asleep.

So, it's something between you and Allah, there's an element of sincerity there, that might not exist with other Ibadaat(عبادات) that are done collectively.

So now, you are doing this alone, nobody can see you, you are not showing off, who are you doing it for?

You are doing it for Allah.

So, it's very important for one, to spend this time in solitude to purify the heart.

Because the scholars say that too much socialization, too much laughing, too much attachment to Duniyah(دُنِيَّا), obscures the heart and throws veils on it.

And the way to purify the heart is by spending some time worshipping Allah سبحانه وتعالى in solitude.

And Allah سبحانه وتعالى says about Taffakkur(تفكر): Behold, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day,

there are indeed signs for men of understanding.

Men who celebrate the praises of Allah standing, sitting and laying down or lying down on their sides, and contemplate the wonders of creation in the heavens and the earth with the thought,

Our Lord, not for not has though created all this.

Glory to You, give us salvation from the chastisement of the fire.

So, Allah سبحانه وتعالى is saying here that His servants contemplate in the creation of the heavens and earth.

And they say: O Allah no, You have not created this in vain.

There's purpose in creation, there's wisdom in everything that exist.
parts.arabic:
اَعُوْذُ بِاللهِ مِنَّ الشِّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيْمِ۞

بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَانِ الرَّحِيْمَ۞

اَلْحَمْدُ لله ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلى سَيِّدِنَا محمد وَعَلَى اَلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ تَسْلِيْمًا كَثِيْرا لِإِيلَافِ قُرَيْشٍ۝إِيلَافِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ الشِّتَاءِ وَالصَّيْفِ۝

فَلْيَعْبُدُوا رَبَّ هَٰذَا الْبَيْتِ۝الَّذِي أَطْعَمَهُمْ مِنْ جُوعٍ وَآمَنَهُمْ مِنْ خَوْفٍ۝

وَإِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَا مَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَاكِ وَطَهَّرَكِ وَاصْطَفَاكِ عَلَىٰ نِسَاءِ الْعَالَمِينَ۝

وَإِذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِي أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَاتَّقِ اللَّهَ وَاتَّقِ اللَّهَ وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ مَا اللَّهُ مُبْدِيهِ وَتَخْشَى النَّاسَ

وَتَخْشَى النَّاسَ وَاللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ تَخْشَاهُ ۖ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيْدٌ مِنْهَا وَطَرًا زَوَّجْنَاكَهَا لِكَيْ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ

لِكَيْ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ فِي أَزْوَاجِ أَدْعِيَائِهِمْ إِذَا قَضَوْا مِنْهُنَّ وَطَرًا ۚ وَكَانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ مَفْعُولًاَ۝

رُعْيَ الْاَنْبِيَاءَ وَحِيْ قَدْ نَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُ لَيَحْزُنُكَ الَّذِي يَقُولُونَ ۖ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ وَلَٰكِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ۝

وَبْنَتُكَ تَصْلُحُلِيْ وَعَسَىٰ أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ ۖ يُطْعِمُ جَآئِعَكُمْ وَيُعَلِّمْ جَاهِلَكُمْ وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا ۖ

إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ۝

إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ مُبَارَكًا وَهُدًى لِلْعَالَمِينَ۝

اَلْاَسْمَاءُ الصِّفَاتْ اَلْصَادِقُ الْاَمِيْن رَضِيْنَه رَضِيْنَهْ Quraish(قُرَيْشْ).

إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ لَآيَاتٍ لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ۝

الَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ

رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَٰذَا بَاطِلًا سُبْحَانَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ۝

صَلَّى الله عَلى سَيَّدِنَا محمد وَعَلى اَلِهِ وَ صَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ تَسْلِيْمًا كَثِيْرًا

docs.title: Seerah of Muhammad Part 5 of 53 VIDEO

parts.english:
Session four; The situation in Arabia and the world, was very desperate.

And for more information in that regard, you could refer to an excellent book, written by Shaikh Abul Hassan Nadawi(شيخ ابو الحسن ندوي) called

What has the world lost by the downfall of the Muslims.?

He has a whole chapter in his book talking about the situation in the world, at the time of Rasool Allah ﷺ.

Over here we just have situation in Arabia.

But over there he talks about the situation in the Persian Empire, China, India, Roman Empire, all around the world.

And it was in a very desperate state, it needed the light of Prophet-hood.

It wasn't entirely evil, people around the world, still retained some good qualities.

And Al-Bootie(البوطي) he talks about some of the good qualities that the non believers of the Arabs had, in the time of Muhammadﷺ.

And he mentions a few examples like generosity and hospitality, fulfilling of a pledge, pride and denial of shame and injustice, firm will and determination,

perseverance and deliberateness, pure and simple life.

So, these are some aspects that were taken advantage of, by Islam.

You see; the Sahabahرضي الله عنهم, because they held these qualities; they were successful in spreading the religion.

Their generosity and hospitality made them welcome, in the nations they would go to.

I mean, the people around the world would welcome the Sahabahرضي الله عنهم.

They weren't like a despised occupier.

The Sahabah(صحابه) were welcomed in the lands, they went to, the people saw them as a liberating army, that would free them from slavery and the servitude that they were going through.

This held true, for example, when it came to the people of Egypt and the people of Syria, who were ruled by the Romans.

They didn't see the army that is coming in, as displacing another occupying army.

No, they saw them as people, who are liberating them.

And then there was something among the Sahabahرضي الله عنهم, they didn't care for power, and authority.

In many places they would go, they would train among the local people; leadership, and then they would hand it over to them.

The Sahabah(صحابہ) were out to call people to Islam, not to rip their resources, like we had in the colonial era of Europe, and the imperial powers of Europe, France, Britain, Italy, Holland.

I mean, they went all over the world, these European powers went all over the world, taking advantage of the people and stripping them of their wealth.

That wasn't the case with the armies of Sahabahرضي الله عنهم.

Their fulfillment of pledges, their firmness and determination.

They were strong, you could count on them, they were powerful, when they gave a word, they would stick to it.

So, these were qualities that were very important for Da'wah(دعوة).

And that's why Allahسبحانه وتعالى chose that particular area to host the last message.

I mean, it wasn't a haphazard thing.

That Allahسبحانه وتعالى chose Makkah, to be the birthplace of Rasool Allah ﷺ.

The people in that area at that time had qualities, which made them the fittest, to carry the message, and they pledged their lives for it, and they gave their lives, they sacrificed everything for Islam.

Anyway, we talked last time about the story of the elephant, Al-Fiel(ألفيل).

Rasool Allah ﷺ was born in Aam-El-Fiel(عام الفيل).

He was born in the year in which Allahسبحانه وتعالى destroyed the army of Abraha(أبراهة).

There are many stories mentioned referring to the birth of Rasool Allah ﷺ miracles that happened.

And you could go into other books to study these stories.

We're not going to go through them for the simple reason that I'm trying to stick to a certain standard of narration, and these stories are usually weak.

Rasool Allah ﷺ when his mother, Aamna(آمنه) was pregnant, Abdullah(عبدالله) his father was on a journey to Ash-Sham(الشام).

But he ended up dying close to Madina and he was buried there.

So, he died before the birth of Muhammadﷺ.

Rasool Allah ﷺ was born and his mother saw a light that is coming out of her, and this light is reaching towards Ash-sham(الشام).

And that was interpreted as the light of the message of Muhammadﷺ reaching to the world.

Rasool Allah ﷺ says about his lineage.

There's a few Ahadith(احاديث) that we'll state, first of all Allahسبحانه وتعالى says; Allah knows best where to place His Prophet Hood.

So, Allahسبحانه وتعالى chose the best to be His Messenger, Muhammadﷺ Now, Imam Ahmad(امام احمد) narrates a Hadith(حديث), that people were talking different things about Muhammadﷺ,

for example they said that Muhammadﷺ was like a green tree grown in a desert.

What they were trying to say, is that Muhammadﷺ was the only good person among his clan.

So, Ibn Abbas(إبن عباس) says certain things the people were saying reached the Messenger of Allah.

So, he mounted the pulpit and asked: "Who am I.?

They replied and said; You are the Messenger of Allah.

He replied; I am Muhammad Bin AbdAllah Bin Abdul Muttalib(محمد بن عبدالله بن عبدالمطلب),  which means son, I am Muhammad(محمد), son of Abdallah(عبد الله), son of Abdul Muttalib(عبدالمطلب),

Allah divides the creation and made me part of His best creatures.

He made them all into two groups, placing me in the better of them, He created the tribes and place me in the best, sub divided them into clans and placed me in the best one,

I am the best of you both in clan and in spirit.

Rasool Allah ﷺ is saying that I am not a good person among a group of evil people.

He said: I am the best but I'm also from among the best.

So, my clan and my tribe are the most noble.

Rasool Allah ﷺ also says; "Verily Allah granted eminence to Kanana(كنانه) from amongst the descendants of Ismail(إسماعيل), and he granted eminence to the Quraish(قريش) from among Kanana(كنانه),

and he granted eminence to the Banni Hashim(بني هاشم) among Quraish(قريش), and he granted me eminence from the tribe of Bannu Hashim( بنو هاشم)."

So Rasool Allah ﷺ was the greatest from among Bannu Hashim(بنو هاشم), and Bannu Hashim(بنو هاشم) was the most noble among Quraish(قُرَيْشْ),

and Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) was the most noble among Kinanaa(كنانه), and Kinanaa(كنانه) was the most noble of the descendants of Ismail(اِسْماعِيْل).

Now, Rasool Allah ﷺ says in another Hadith(حديث), I was the product of true marriage, not fornication from Adam(آدم), right on up to when my father and my mother had me,

I was not at all tainted by the fornication of Jahilliyah(جاهليه).

In the time Jahilliyah(جاهليه), because of the corruption and lewdness that occurs, when people are far away from the true message, their hearts become perverted.

And a lot of immoral acts occur among the people.

Rasool Allah ﷺ is saying; Even though part of my ancestry lived in those eras, in those times, but I was a product of marriage all the way up to Adam(آدم).

So, there isn't any, of my ancestors, who had a relationship of Zina(زنا), it is all through marriage, all the way to Adam عليه السلام, and that is something that Allah has granted to Muhammadﷺ.

It was all through true marriage.

I hope the meaning of this is clear that, the lineage of Rasool Allah ﷺ from him all the way up to Adam عليه السلام, was a product of marriage.

The famous names of Muhammadﷺ that we know are Muhammad(محمد) and Ahmad(احمد) but he has some additional names, and we'll talk about the meanings of these names.

The name that was given to him by his parents was Muhammadﷺ, and who was the one, who named him Muhammad(محمد).?

Who was it.?

His grandfather, Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) is the one, who named him Muhammadﷺ.

Now the name Muhammad(محمد) means to be eternally praised.

For he, ﷺ obliges praise from people for his characteristics, his sayings, his actions, and he is the embodiment of praise and he is therefore Muhammad(محمد).

So, Muhammad(محمد) means a person, who draws praise.

Muhammadﷺ, as we mentioned earlier, is praised eternally.

Allahسبحانه وتعالى has fulfilled the meaning of his name.

There is no human being that ever lived in history, who was praised like Muhammadﷺ.

He is praised day and night.

AHMAD(احمد), the name Ahmad(احمد) comes from the same root, see, Muhammad(محمد) and Ahmad(احمد) come from the root Hamd(حمد), and what does Hamd(حمد) mean, praise.

When you say Al-Hamdolillah(ألحمداالله), Praise be to Allah.

So, both the name Muhammad(محمد) and Ahmad(احمد) are derived from the same root.

Muhammad(محمد) means a person who draws praise, so he is praised.

Ahmad(احمد) means that he praises Allah.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ is the most among us in praising Allahسبحانه وتعالى.

So, there is no person that ever lived, who praises Allahعَزّوجَلّ like Muhammadﷺ.

So, here you have two meanings, Muhammad(محمد) means he is the most praised.

Ahmad(احمد), he praises Allah, the Most.

These are the two famous names of Muhammadﷺ.

But he has also told us, some of his other names and these are from Ahadith(احاديث).

One of his other names is Al-Haashir(ألحاشر).

Al-Haashir(ألحاشر) means the gatherer to whom humanity will be resurrected in his wake.

The Prophet ﷺ is the first to be resurrected among the creation, then mankind will be resurrected following him.

So, the first person to be resurrected will be Muhammadﷺ, and then people will come after that.

So, he is the first on the Day of Judgment.

Al-Muqaffie(ألْمُقَفِّيْ), the successor, for he ﷺ is the last of the Prophets and Messengers and there shall be none succeeding him.

So, Muhammadﷺ is the last, Al-Muqaffie(ألْمُقَفِّيْ), is the last.

Al-Mahee(اَلْمَاحِيْ), the eraser that erases and eradicates Kuffr(كفر).

There is no Prophet that will succeed in eliminating Kuffr(كفر) entirely, except Muhammadﷺ.

Now, that mission has not been fulfilled yet because his Ummah(امة) is still carrying on that mission, but the eventual victory of Islam, which will be the combination of human history,

will be a moment of time when the whole world will be Muslim.

And that will be carried on by the Ummah(امة) of  Muhammadﷺ under the leadership of Eesa عليه السلام Jesus May peace be upon him.

So, Muhammadﷺ is the one, who will be successful in eradicating, erasing Kuffr(كفر) from the face of the earth.

So, he's called Al-Maahi(ألماحي) he will erase and eradicate Kuffr(كفر), one of his other names is Nabi-Ul-Malhamah(نبي الملحمه), the Prophet of the fierce battle.

Now, Malhamah(ملحمه) is a fierce battle and it's also a series of battles.

Rasool Allah ﷺ was named the Prophet of Al-Malhamah(الملحمه), the Prophet of the fierce battles.

One can give different interpretation to that, one meaning is that his Ummah(امة) are the greatest in terms of Jihad(جهاد).

There is no Ummah(امة), that has fought Jihad(جهاد), like the Ummah(امة) of Muhammadﷺ.

That's one meaning.

Another meaning that could be drawn from this name of Rasool Allah ﷺ, that the future of humanity after Muhammadﷺ will be that a very fierce battles.

And we have seen examples of that in World War One and World War Two.

History is divided into stages.

We're now living in the state of Muhammadﷺ, which extends until the Day of Judgment.

So, events that are happening now, even though they might not be done by Muslims, but we are still living in the era of Muhammadﷺ.

And everyone living on the face of the earth is part of the Ummah(امة) of Muhammadﷺ, in the sense that he is their Prophet.

Now whether they accept it or not is a different question.

But they are part of his Ummah(امة) and they will come on the day of Judgment and they will be asked about who.?

They won't be asked Eesa(عيسى), they won't be asked about Musa(موسى) they will be asked about Muhammadﷺ, did you follow him or not?

Rasool Allah ﷺ was nursed initially by his mother, and Umm Ayman(أم أيمن) whose name is Barakah(بركة).

And Umm Ayman(ام ايمن) is an Abyssinian, woman who lived in Makkah.

She later on became Muslim, and Rasool Allah ﷺ and married her to his emancipated slave, Zaid Bin Harissa(زيد بن حارثه).

Zaid Bin Harissa(زيد بن حارثه) was a slave, Rasool Allah ﷺ freed him, and he married him to Umm Ayman(ام ايمن).

So, she also nursed him.

It was a tradition among the urban Arabs, to send their children, to grow up in the desert.

They used to believe that the desert is more pure and is a cleaner environment and is healthier for them, to grow in.

They also believe that this will strengthen their character because of the harshness, it will make them stronger people.

So, they would send their children out of the cities to live in the desert.

And that happened with Rasool Allah ﷺ, he was brought up in the land of Bannu Sa'ad(بنو سعد), Halima Sadia(حليمه سعديه) narrates to us this story.

She says that she came with her friends to Makkah, so that they could take with them children to nurse.

And for them, this was something that they were paid for.

So, you would have these Bedouin women come into Makkah and they will try to adopt or nurse some children.

Halima Sadia(حليمه سعديه) came into Makkah.

And she said that, that particular year was the year of famine, so they were very poor.

Now, she and her friends they went around the houses of Makkah, searching for children, who need to be nursed.

She said that Muhammadﷺ was presented to each and every one of them and they all declined to accept him.

They all refused to accept Muhammadﷺ.

Why.?

Because he was an orphan.

They were saying what good is an orphan, who will pay us.?

If his father is dead.

So, they wouldn't agree on a certain amount of money.

What they will do is they would nurse the child and then they will be given some financial compensation as a gift.

Since Muhammadﷺ was an orphan, no one accepted him because he doesn't have a father to pay for him.

And they said his mother wouldn't really be able to pay us much, so they all declined to accept Muhammadﷺ.

Halima(حليمه) says at the end of the day, all of my friends were going back to their camps with children except myself, I found no one to take with me.

So, at night, I told my husband, I'm going to go next day in the morning and accept that child called Muhammad(محمد), since we have no one else,

I'm not going to go back home empty handed.

She said my husband agreed.

So, I want next day in the morning and I went to Muhammad(محمد)'s mother, Aamna Bint Wahb(آمنه بنت وهب) and I said that I accept to take your child.

Halima(حليمه) says that the night before we couldn't get any sleep because our camel was not providing any milk.

And because of the famine and the hunger, I wasn't able to provide my own child with milk.

So, he would cry throughout the night and keep us awake.

That was their situation, very poor.

Halima(حليمه) says; that as soon as I picked up Muhammadﷺ and took him back to my camp.

My breast immediately welcomed him and provided him with all the milk that he needed, until he was satisfied and the milk was enough for my son.

And that was the first night that we were able to get a full night of sleep because my son wasn't able to sleep for quite a few nights.

So, immediately the Barakah(بركة) of Muhammadﷺ was apparent.

She said, and then my husband went out to milk the camel and it was providing so much milk that my husband came back and said: O Halima(حليمه),

you have brought us a blessed soul, there's something going on.

All of this blessing is showering us since you brought this young child in our house.

So, now they're still camping in Makkah, and they're ready now to go back, to the desert.

Halima(حليمه) said that when we were coming to Makkah I was riding a donkey that was so old and weak, it was slowing down the whole group, and it was annoying everybody else.

She said, that this donkey was old and weak.

You know, sometimes you'd have a donkey rather than going straight, it would go sideways, very tired and disoriented.

She said when we were going back my donkey was the fastest among the group.

She said, my friends were asking me.?

Is this the same animal you brought with you?

When we came to Makkah? She said: Yes.

They said by Allah, something is going on.

Now, they went back to their land.

Halima(حليمه) said; Me and my husband would send out our goats to graze, they would come back full, and we would milk them whenever we want.

While everybody else in our tribe, their animals would be hungry without any milk.

Now people are starting to complain to the shepherds telling them, why don't you go and graze the animals the same place, where Halima(حليمه) is grazing hers.

She said; So they would take their animals after us, following us to the same place, yet ours would come back full and their's would comeback empty.

And she said the child was growing up, and we were seeing the blessings of Allah on all of us, because of him.

She says, there's a statement here.

And God went on blessing us this way, and we recognized it, then he reached two years of age, he was already growing up a very fine boy.

Not like the other children.

I swear that by the age of two, he was a sturdy boy.

So, we took him to his mother, when he was two years old.

Now it's time for them to return the child.

That's it.

And Subhaan Allah(سبحان الله), it seems that the Arabs of Makkah learned that the city is not a very healthy environment especially with Makkah.

Because it receives a lot of visitors from all over Arabia, you know, they could bring with them different diseases and germs into town.

But the desert is very pure.

The desert is hot and dry and that makes it an unsuitable environment for the growth of bacteria.

And it would be a very healthy place to be.

So, now at the age of two, it was time for them to return Muhammadﷺ to his mother.

They went to Makkah, they told Aamna(آمنه); we want to keep, Muhammad(محمد) with us.

You know, it's not good for him to be in Makkah, and it might be dangerous.

They were bringing up all of these excuses.

They wanted to keep Muhammadﷺ and they loved him so much, they knew that he's blessed.

They wanted to keep him and they kept on trying, and trying, and trying, until Aamna(آمنه) agreed.

Subhaan(سبحان الله) that was the blessing of Allah following Muhammadﷺ.

She eventually agreed.

So, they took him back with them.

One day Muhammadﷺ was playing with his foster brother.

So, his foster brother came in rushing and said; my brother from Quraish(قُرَيْشْ).

They said, What happened to him?

He said, Two men dressed in white, came down and knocked him to the ground, and then they opened up his abdomen.

So, Halima(حليمه) said, Me and his father went rushing, and we came to see Muhammadﷺ, his color was pale, and we asked him what happened?

He said: Two men came and they opened my chest.

And they took out something from it.

Halima(حليمه), she loves Muhammad(محمد) so much.

And she didn't want anything to harm him.

Plus, she didn't want anything bad to happen to him when he is with her.

So, she rushed back to Makkah and went to Aamna(آمنه) and said; Here is Muhammad(محمد) you can now have him, we have fulfilled our responsibility.

Aamna(آمنه) said: How come you're bringing him back when you are so interested in keeping him?

They said, nothing.

She insisted.

She said, Tell me what happened?

You were so insistent on keeping him and now you want to bring him back, What happened?

Halima(حليمه) said; she kept on questioning us, until we eventually told her.

Aamna(آمنه) responded and said; Are you afraid for him, that Satan might hurt him?

By Allah that will not happen.!

When I was pregnant with him, it was the lightest pregnancy and when I delivered him, his birth was unlike any other child, and when he came out, I have seen light that was reaching to Ash-Sham(الشام).

So, the protection of Allah is with him, and I'm sure that he will have a great future.

So, now Muhammadﷺ was back with his mother.

His mother passed away when he was at the age of six.

So, now he lost his father and mother.

He was adopted by his grandfather Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب), who raised him up and Abdul Muttalib(عبدالمطلب) passed away when Muhammadﷺ was at the age of eight.

And now, Muhammadﷺ was taken care of, by his uncle Abu Talib(ابو طالب), who protected him, and helped him, and supported him, for the next 40 years, in the life of Muhammadﷺ.

This is the early years of صلوات الله وسلام عليه.

We'll talk about a few events here and there, that happened before Prophet hood.

We're not going to spend much time on the Pre Prophet hood era, but we'll talk about the important events that happened.

Rasool Allah ﷺ was protected by Allah, he would not commit sins, which were usual and normal amongst his people.

Allahسبحانه وتعالى was keeping him away from these sins.

Rasool Allah ﷺ narrates, an example of this.

In the house of Rasool Allah ﷺ.

Muhammadﷺ.

So, they're hired by someone else.

So, they have to report to a higher authority, they have to report to someone else.

Now, a shepherd cannot go back to the owner and say; Well, I'm sorry, I lost one sheep, because that sheep happened to be stupid.

Anything that happens to this flock.

Even if the sheep was wrong, you are responsible for it.

you can't go back and say, well, the sheep was wrong.

It's not my fault.

No, it's your fault.

So, they learn to be responsible for herd, even if the herd is not responsible for itself.

Whether they're united or not, whether they obey or not, I am accountable for that.

it would attract insects.

you gonna scream to the top of your voice and tell him, Be careful!.

Da'wah(دعوة) is one aspect.

A Daiyah(داعيا) cannot be sincere and whole heartedly involved in Da'wah(دعوة), if they cannot have patience, and they are not willing to go into situations that might be difficult.

The next important event that happened during the early years of Rasool Allah ﷺ, was a pact called Hilf-Al-Fudhool(حلف ألفضول).

The story behind this is there was a man who came in from Zabeed(زبيد), in Yemen.

He came to do business in Makkah.

His merchandise was taken by Al-Aas Bin Wael(ألعاص بن وائل), who promised to pay him back.

He's gonna sell it and pay him back.

Al-Aas Bin Wael(ألعاص بن وائل), after a while refused to pay this man, he was taken advantage of the fact that he's a foreigner, he's not from Makkah.

He told them, frankly, I'm not gonna pay you.

Al-Aas(العاص) expected that this man will just walk away.

I mean, he's, he's a foreigner who will help him.

But the man didn't.

The man stood up for his right.

And he went to a public place in Makkah.

And he started calling the people of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ).

And he was telling them I was oppressed in your land.

And, are you people who are going to stand up for my rights?

Will you allow this oppression to happen in your land?

And he said a few emotional words.

So, some of the clans of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) decided to meet together to bring about an agreement on protecting the rights of the weak in Makkah,

we cannot allow this to happen.

And among these families of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ), was the family of Rasool Allah ﷺ, his uncle's.

Rasool Allah ﷺ at the time was a young boy.

But he said my uncle's took me with them to attend this meeting.

The meeting was held in the house of Abdullah Bin Jad'aan(عبدالله بن جدعان).

Abdullah Bin Jad'aan(عبدالله بن جدعان), this was symbolic for them to have it in his house, because he was a man who was very generous, very kind to others.

And he was a person, who was stand up for what is right.

So, they decided to honor him by having this meeting in his house.

So, they So they came together and they made an agreement that we will stand together all of us, present here.

We will stand together to protect the rights of the oppressed and the weak.

This happened before Prophet hood.

It was a pact that occurred between non believers, between Mushrikeen(مشركين).

Rasool Allah ﷺ said: I witnessed in the house of Abdullah Bin Jad'aan(عبدالله بن جدعان).

A pact made that I wouldn't have exchanged it for the choicest-heart.

And if it had been suggested after Islam, I would have responded positively to it.

Rasool Allah ﷺ is saying that, if I'm invited to it today, after the message of Islam, has been given to me, I would have still responded to it, even though it was held by non believers.

The important lesson to learn from this is that Muslims should side with what is right, no matter what the source is, no matter where that is coming from.

Muslims should stand for human rights, should stand for the oppressed, should stand for the needy, no matter what their religious background is.

We should stand up for what is good.

As a Muslim, we stand up for what is right.

And Rasool Allah ﷺ was making this point by stating that I would respond to it today if I was invited.

The man was given back what belongs to him, after that.

An incident happened later on, in the time of Al-Amwi'een(ألأمويين) we're talking about a few decades after Rasool Allah ﷺ passed away.

It's happened between Al-Hussain Bin Ali(الحسين بن علي) the son of Ali Ibn Abi Talib(علي ابن ابي طالب) and Al-Waleed Bin Ut'bah Bin Abu Sufiaan(ألوليد بن عتبه بن أبو سفيان), who was the governor of Madina,

because Al-Waleed(الوليد) was the governor of Madina, he was taking advantage of his position.

And he has taken away some property that belongs to the son of Ali Ibn Abi Talib(علي ابن ابي طالب), Al-Hussain(ألحسين).

Al-Hussain(الحسين) what he did is.?

He went to, Al-Waleed(الوليد) and told him you either give me back what belongs to me.

Otherwise, I'm gonna walk into the Masjid(مسجد) and invite the people to Hil-Ful Fudhool(حلف ألفضول) I'm gonna remind them about Hil-Ful Fudhool(حلف ألفضول).

Now, Abdullah Bin Zubair(عبدالله بن زبير) was with Al-Waleed(الوليد) at that time.

And he said: "And I too swear by Allah, that if he does invoke it, I draw my sword and stand there with him, until he gets his justice or we'll all die together."

And then some other people heard about that Al-Musawwir Bin Makramah(ألمصور بن مكرمه) and Abdur Rahman Bin Usman Bin Ubaid(عبدالرحمن بن عثمان بن عبيد)

and others and they gave similar statements.

So now, it was picking up and Al-Waleed(الوليد) realized that it could become quite dangerous.

So, he gave back Al-Hussain(الحسين), what belongs to him.

The reason why I'm bringing this in, even though it happened way after Seerah(سيرة), the life of Rasool Allah ﷺ is, to show that Muslims would not allow wrong to happen in front of them.

I mean, here you have people who are living under a particular leader, Al-Waleed Bin Utba(الوليد بن عتبه).

Nevertheless, they stood up and they protected their brother, who was in need, even if they had to give up their lives.

So, Muslim should stand up for what is right.

Shaikh Muhammad Al-Ghazali(شيخ محمد الغزالي), He comments on this pact he says; This pact shows that no matter how dark life becomes, and oppressive dictators become

noble characteristics will still remain in certain people, who stand up for justice and Birr(بِرّ), Birr(بِرّ) is righteousness.

Allah has made cooperation in enjoying good an obligation upon Muslims, which He has called to, in the verse and cooperate in virtue and taqwa(تقوي)

and do not help one another in sin and transgression.

So, for a group of Muslims to enter into a treaty or a contract, such as the aforementioned is made permissible because it is only a reinforcement for an Islamic obligation.

However, this by definition must be dissimilar to the situation of Masjid Zarrar(مسجد الضرار).

This was a mosque created in Madina to exclude groups of Muslims.

He says, where the cooperation turns into a nationalistic or elitist strategy to exclude Muslims.

As for the Muslims, contracting with the people of other faiths, in order to remove oppression or to face an oppressor, this becomes permissible for them,

if there is in it, the welfare of Islam and Muslims in the present and the future.

The basis for this is essentially the Prophets ﷺ willingness to answer the call for the pact even after Islam.
