assets.title: #3. The Religious Situation Of Pre Islamic Arabia

parts.english:
The Life Of Muhammadﷺ, The Makkan Period By Imam Anwar Al-Awlaki This is our third session.

In Sha Allah(ان شاءالله) we will talk about the religious background of Arabia, so that we know the environment in which Rasool Allah ﷺ lived.

Now, obviously they started on Touheed(توحيد) because of the Da'wah(دعوة) of Ismail عليه السّلام.

He was their Prophet, and they followed him.

So, the Arabs of Arabia started out as Muslims as believers in the oneness of Allah.

So, what went wrong, down the line for them to reach to the level they were at, when Rasool Allah ﷺ was sent to them.

In the time of Rasool Allah ﷺ there were three religions in Arabia, idol worshipping, Christianity and Judaism.

So, we'll talk about how these three religions came into existence.?

Amr Bin Lohae Al-Khuza'e(عمرو بن لوحي الخزاعي), you remember him, he is the leader of Khuza'a(خزاعه).

This man was very generous, very strong, very much respected by his people.

They used to respect him so much, and admire him, so much that his words were taken as law.

Amr Bin Lohae Al-Khuza'e(عمرو بن لوحي الخزاعي), he traveled to Syria, to Ash-sham(الشام).

And I'm translating Ash-sham(الشام) as Syria, even though it's not the correct translation, I mean Ash-sham(الشام) refers to Syria, Phalastine(فلسطين), Lebanon(لبنان) and Jordan.

That land is called Ash-sham(الشام).

And the center of Ash-sham(الشام) is Jerusalem, Bait-Ul-Maqdis(بيت المقدس).

But it has been translated in English and Syria, so we'll just go by that translation, for now.

So, here we have Amr Bin Lohae Al-Khuza'e(عمرو بن لوحي الخزاعي), he is traveling to Ash-sham(الشام) to Syria.

He goes there, and he finds these idols, so he asked the people, What are these.?

So, they told him: Well, these are intermediates between us and Allah.

So, when want to ask for rain, we asked them, they appeal on our behalf to Allah.

When we want children, we would go to different idol, when we want this, you'd go to that idol, in war we have a certain idol.

And they appeal on our behalf to God and they perform things for us.

Amr Bin Lohae (عمرو بن لوحي) said: Excellent, this is what we need.!

That is what we need, we need someone to appeal to our Lord to provide us with rain, to provide us with wealth.

How about, you hand me over one of these idols, so I can take it back home.

So, they gave him a pretty good idol, big huge called Hubal(حُبَلْ).

So, he carried Hubal(حُبَلْ) with him back to Makkah.

And he established it, next to Al-Ka'aba(الكعبه), in Al-Haram(الحرم).

And he told his people, these will intercede on your behalf to Allahسبحانه وتعالى, ask them whatever you want.

Now, Makkah being the center of Arabia the religious authority of Arabia, bringing an idol to Makkah carried with it, such a heavy weight, I mean

you have the Arabs coming from all over the peninsula to make Hajj(حج).

So, all of them were exposed to this new Bid'dah(بدعة), innovation in religion.

And it started spreading like wildfire.

Because it was coming from the religious center.

And it was also adopted by Amr Bin Lohae Al-Khuza'e(عمرو بن لوحي الخزاعي), who was so respected by his people.

So now, it became a business, in Makkah they would make idols to export to the other tribes.

So now, every tribe would come to Makkah and they would carry with them an idol to take home, because they cannot come all the time and ask from Hubal(حُبَلْ).

So, they would have these idols that they would carry with them.

And then this concept was developed further, I mean, it starts out small and then it grows.

The concept was carried further, so now they were making portable idols, you carry it in your backpack wherever, you're traveling you have one with you.

I don't know, if you remember the story of Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب).

He was one seen crying and laughing, so he was asked: Why were you crying and why were you laughing.?

He said the reason why I was laughing is.

I remembered in the time of Jahilliyah(جاهليه), in the time of ignorance.

I was traveling, and I wanted to pray.

But then I remember that I forgot to bring my god with me.

So, what I did is, I tried to think of a way, I want to pray.

So, I had some dates with me.

So I molded the dates into a form of an idol, and I worshiped it.

Later on, that night I became hungry.

So, I ate my idol.

He said, that's why I'm laughing.

You know, now he's looking back and he is saying, what was I doing, how could I do that.?

You see how Islam changed, see how Islam changed them.

See, who was Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) and who he became after Islam.

You know, these giants Sahabah(صحابه), when you read about them and their wisdom, this is where they were.

So, this shows you how Islam had the power to change them from being nothing, to being the best, how Islam transformed them in a very short period, that's a miracle.

That's a miracle of Islam that it had the capacity to bring such a people, and to bring about in their lives such a change, and make out of them, these giants.

I mean Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب), who would Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) be without Islam.?

Abbas Mahmood Al-Aqqaad(عباس محمود ألعقاد), he asked that question, in his book about Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب), he says, who would Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) be without Islam.

He said: Maybe he could grow to become the leader of his clan, his family of Bannu Udae(بنوعُدَيْ) which were a very small branch of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ).

He said, or maybe he could have been one of the prominent leaders of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ).

Or if we extend it further than he might be the head of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ), which is a farfetched assumption because the other clans of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ),

who held power in the past, would never allow such a thing to happen, to start with.

So, he said, we're stretching it too far to say that he would become a leader over Quraish(قُرَيْشْ).

He said: But the most likely scenario was that Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) would die at a young age, he used to drink a lot before Islam.

So, most likely he would have died at a young age, and Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) would have been an obscure figure of history.

But with Islam, not only he become a leader of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) or Arabia, he became the ruler of two thirds of the world at that time.

One of the greatest men that ever lived in history.

That is the transformation that Islam brought in their lives.

Anyway, so idols were being exported and now they were being made in different shapes and forms and you have a different idol for a different purpose

and Al-Ka'aba(الكعبه) was polluted, surrounded with idols.

Three HUndred and sixty(360) idols surrounding Al-Ka'aba(الكعبه).

Shirk(شرك) now was in every direction, What started out as one idol imported turned into a huge exporting business and Shirk(شرك) it in every direction in Makkah.

So, that is how the religion of Ismail(اِسْماعِيْل) changed down the line.

Rasool Allah ﷺ says: Rasool Allah ﷺ says: I have seen Amr Bin Lohae Al-Khuza'e(عمرو بن لوحي الخزاعي) dragging his entrails, his intestines in hellfire,

because he was the first man to change the religion of the Arabs.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ said: I saw him in Hellfire, going around his intestines trying to pull them back in his stomach.

So, this is how idol worshipping was introduced in Arabia.

What about the Jewish faith and Christianity.?

The King of Yemen, Tabbana Sa'ad(تَبَّانَه سَعْدْ) was traveling to do business in Ash-sham(الشام).

And he passed next to Al-Madina, and he left his son in Madina to do business, until he comes back from Syria.

The people of Madina killed his son.

So, when Tabbana Sa'ad(تَبَّانَه سَعْدْ) came back and heard the news that his son was killed.

He decided to destroy Madina.

So, he attacked and his army was overwhelming, compared to the small armies of Madina, so he could have crushed, his opposition.

But two Jewish rabbis came out of Madina.

Now how did Jews get there in the first place.?

When the Romans destroyed Jerusalem, the Jews dispersed, there were some of them, who came down into Arabia.

In search of the promised land where the Nabbi(نبي) would be sent.

Because they had in their books signs of the awaited prophet.

So, they were looking for the place where he would immigrate to.

They saw these signs in Madina and in a few other places, in Hajar(حجر), and other places.

So, and this is where the Jews settled.

Because these places, had the resemblances or the signs of the place where the Prophet would be sent.

So, that is why they settled in Madina.

Three Jewish tribes, we had Bannu Qainuqah(بنو قَینُقاع), Bannu Nadhir(ببنو نضير) and Bannu Quraidha(بنو قريظه).

So, that's how they reached Madina, so they were ethnically Jewish, who emigrated when the Romans sacked Jerusalem.

So, these two Jewish rabbis they came out, and they came to Tabbana Sa'ad(تَبَّانَه سَعْدْ) and they told him, This place is protected by God, if you attempt to destroy it, Allah will destroy you.

And they were able to convince Tabbana Sa'ad(تَبَّانَه سَعْدْ).

Tabbana Sa'ad(تَبَّانَه سَعْدْ) not only agreed to withdraw his army and stop attacking Madina, but he also was impressed by their religion and wanted to become Jewish himself.

And then he invited these two Jewish rabbis to go with him to Yemen, and they agreed, and he became Jewish.

Now, on his way south, heading back to Yemen.

The tribe of Hawazin(هوازن), they had a problem between them and Quraish(قُرَيْشْ), Hawazin(هوازن), they had a problem with the people of Makkah.

So, they wanted to make a Fitnah(فِتْنَه) to start a division or cause a problem between Tabbana Sa'ad(تَبَّانَه سَعْدْ) and Makkah and they succeeded.

So, Tabbana Sa'ad(تَبَّانَه سَعْدْ) was contemplating attacking Makkah.

Now these two Jewish rabbis told him, This is another town that is protected by Allah, you shouldn't attack Makkah, in fact, he should go into Makkah and make Tawwaf(طواف) around Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

He said: Well, let's go.

They said: No, we cannot join you.

How come.?

They said: We are scholars and it is not appropriate for us, as scholars to go and make Tawwaf(طواف) around Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), when it's surrounded by Idols.

So, he went in and he made Tawwaf(طواف), and the Tabbana Sa'ad(تَبَّانَه سَعْدْ) was the first person ever to cloth Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

He was the first one to clothe Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

And he would cloth it, once a year.

And the way they would do it in the past is.?

They would bring the new clothing and place it over the old, because they considered, the clothing of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) to be sacred and they can take it off.

So, they would keep on piling up one cloth over another, until the sheer weight of it was so heavy.

Eventually they decided that they're going to have to take it off, and just place one clothing at a time.

Tabbana Sa'ad(تَبَّانَه سَعْدْ) then went with these two Jewish rabbis to Yemen and they were given freedom and encouragement to spread the religion, among the Yemeni tribes.

And many of the tribes in Yemen did embrace the Jewish faith.

So, you have two types of Jews in Arabia.

You have ethnic Jews in Khaybar(خيبر) and Madina but then you have Jews by conversion, in Yemen.

So, the Jews of Yemen, are ethnically Arab, but they adopted the Jewish faith.

So, you can see that at some moments of time, Jews did preach their religion, and now they might not do that but there were points in history where they did, preach their religion to others,

and an example is, Yemen.

So, that's how the Jewish religion was introduced into Arabia.

What about Christianity.?

When Eesa عليه السّلام was sent some of his followers dispersed in the land and Christianity was dividing into many sects very early on.

And very early on, many of these sects became disbelievers.

They were Dhalah(ضلاله), misguidance was introduced very early on into the sects of Christianity.

However, there were pockets of believers here and there that were able to retain the true Christian faith, that was preached by Syedina Eesa(سيدناعيسى), Jesus عليه السّلام,

believing in the oneness of Allah, believing that Eesa(عيسى) is as a messenger of Allah, rather than being the son of God.

These were concepts that were retained by some of the Christians around the world.

One of these men made it into Yemen, and started preaching in the area of Najraan(نجران).

And their religion was spreading but secretly and privately and slowly.

By that time Tabbana Sa'ad(تَبَّانَه سَعْدْ) was dead.

And the king of Yemen was his son, Abu Nawaas(ابو نواس) or Du Nawaas(ذو نواس).

News of this new religion reached to the king, and he banned it, and he persecuted the followers.

There is the story in Sahih Muslim(صحيح مسلم) of the king, and the young boy.

Many scholars would attribute this story to the events between Du Nawwas(ذو نواس) and the Christians in Yemen, it would say that the king was Du Nawwas(ذو نواس),

and that story is in Sahih Muslim(صحيح مسلم) we will go over it.

It says that the king used to deal in magic.

And he had the sorcerer as his advisor.

So, this sorcerer was growing old in age, and he told the king that I might pass away in any moment so I need to train someone, to take my place.

I need to inherit my skills to someone, who would carry on.

So, they tried to find the very bright and intelligent young man and they handpicked a young man and they assigned him as an apprentice with this sorcerer.

So, he was supposed to leave very early on, in the morning from his house and go and study under the sorcerer, and then come back home at night.

Now this young man on his way towards the Saahir(ساحر), the sorcerer, saw a worship place.

And he heard prayers coming in from this place, which were different.

So, he decided to go and visit.

And it was a church of Tauheed(توحيد) of unity of Allah, preaching the true religion of Eesa عليه السلام.

And he was very impressed by what he was hearing.

But he's supposed to be studying with the sorcerer.

So, he asked the priest, he told him: What can I do?

The priests told him, when you leave home visit me and come and study with me and then go to the sorcerer and if he tells you how come you were late.

Tell him, because my parents delayed me.

On your way back visit me.

And when you get home, when your parents tell you how come you're late tell them that the sorcerer delayed me.

So, you could take a class in the morning and take a class at evening.

So, he continued doing that for a while.

One day in the market place.

Certain beasts entered into the market place and cause chaos, among the people and no one was able to deal with it.

So, this young man said: O Allah, today I want to know whether the path of the priest or the path of the sorcerer is the truth.

So, O Allah, show me the truth.

And everyone was attempting to kill this beast and no one succeeded.

And then this boy picked up a rock and he said: O Allah! If the path of the priest is the truth, then kill this animal.

And he threw the rock, and it killed the animal immediately.

He went back and reported this to the priest, he told him what happened.!

The priest told him, my son, today you have achieved, attained a very high status.

Therefore, you would be tested, you will go through trials, no one can reach such a high status without being tested by Allah.

In exams, the better the student, the more difficult the exam should be.

Because you want to tell the difference between the levels of the students.

So, you have easy questions, which everyone is able to answer.

And then you have medium difficulty.

And then you have difficult and then you have very difficult, because you want to distinguish the A plus, from A minus.

You want to tell the difference.

Same thing Allahسبحانه وتعالى has brought us on this earth for a test.

And according to your level, you would be tested.

Rasool Allah ﷺ says: The ones, who go through the most difficult tests are the Ambiyaa(أنبِيَاء).

And then it goes down according to your level.

So, this priest was telling the young man, you will be tested.

And then he told him and when you are tested, do not disclose my name.

Because the priest was doing his Da'wah(دعوة) in secret.

And he doesn't want his name to be exposed.

It is not out of fear, this is for the security of the Da'wah(دعوة).

So, he told him, and when you go through trials, do not mention my name.

And down the road, we’ll see that the priest was a very courageous man.

I mean, he might wonder, why is he saying don't mention my name?

What is he afraid of?

How come he can't just go outside and say: Here I'm a Muslim and invite everybody openly?

Why is he afraid, why is he keeping a secret?

But you will see that the priests was a very courageous man, but he was a wise man too.

The Associate of the king was blind.

And he came to this young man to cure him because now the young man has studied under the sorcerer.

So, now he is the expert people go to him.

So, when he went to the young man, the young man told him; I cannot heal you, but Allah can heal you, Allah can do it, and he healed the man.

So, the blind man who's now cured, went to the king, and the king told him; Who cured you.?

The man said: Allah.

The king said and do you have a god other than me?

The man said: Yes, Allah is my Lord and your Lord.

The king tortured, this friend of his, and told him to disclose the name of the person, who taught him this.

And under the persecution, he gave up the name and said it is the young man or the boy.

Now, they brought in the boy, and they started to torture him.

And the boy under duress, and pain did give up the name of his teacher, the priest.

He could not sustain the pain and suffering that he was going through, so he disclosed the name So, now they brought the priest and they told the priest, to give up his religion.

And he refused.

So, they brought a saw, and they place it on top of his head, and they cut him into two.

But he refused to give up his religion.

This is the courage that he had and this is the perseverance and the patience.

He gave up his life, he was tortured brutally.

But he never gave up his religion.

And now they're left with the boy.

So, the king ordered a group of his soldiers to carry this boy and throw him from the top of a cliff.

They carried the boy and Subhaan Allah(سبحان الله), Allah was performing Karamaat(كرامات) on the hand of this boy.

Karamah(كرامة) is a miracle that would occur to a Non-Prophet.

And miracles happen to the Prophets.

That's the difference between Mujizza(معجزه) and Karamah(كرامة).

Mu'jizah(معجزة) happens to a Prophet and Karama(كرامه) happens to a person, who is not a Prophet, but they are both supernatural events.

So, this boy made Dua(دُعَا) to Allah and said: O Allah O Allah take care of them, the way you want, I'm going to leave it, up to you O Allah take care of them the way you want.

Allahسبحانه وتعالى made them reach, the top of the cliff, and then the cliff started to shake.

And all of the soldiers fell down, except he.

And now the boy is walking back and he entered into the palace of the king, here I am again.

So, the king appointed another group of soldiers to take him, obviously soldiers are disposable with this king.

So, he appointed, the new group of soldiers to take him into a ship.

And when they reach into the deep waters, just throw him in the water.

So, they were on this boat, and he made the same Dua(دعا) again, O Allah take care of them the way you want to.

The boat capsized, and they all drowned, except he, he went back to safety.

So, he went to the king, and the king was ready to appoint a third group of soldiers to take him.

The boy told him wait, you're not going to be able to kill me, unless you do what I tell you.

The King told him, what is it.?

The boy said, you tie me to a tree and you gather everyone and you bring an arrow and you say: Bismillah(بسم الله), the Lord of the boy, then you will be able to kill me.

So, the boy told him the prescription of how to kill him.

And this is one of the many evidences given, for the justification of what is referred to as suicide bombings.

These are one of the evidences that are given that it is allowed.

Obviously there are restrictions on when it is allowed and where.

But the concept itself of a person giving up their life for Allahسبحانه وتعالى is a valid one, based on this evidence, and many others.

Because he told the king, how it is possible to get rid of him.

If he didn't, he would have survived.

So, he basically told the king how to kill him.

But the boy did it for a noble cause.

What happened is the king followed the instructions and publicly said: In the Name of Allah, the Lord of the boy.

And the arrow hit him right in his head, and he immediately died.

But the result of that action was that everyone who attended became Muslim.

So, he did it for Da'wah(دعوة), he gave up his life, so that everyone else would live.

Because the person is dead without Islam.

The advisors of the king told him what you're afraid of happened.

I mean in the whole purpose of killing this boy is, to get rid of this religion and here we are stuck with our whole nation becoming Muslim.

Actually, in this situation Christian but it is Islam, it is the oneness of Allahسبحانه وتعالى.

Abu Nawaas(ابو نواس) instructed his soldiers to dig trenches, after they dig trenches, they filled them with wood, and ignite them.

And anyone who refuses to give up their religion were forced them into the fire.

And they would bring loads of people and burn them alive.

And these are people who were holding firm to their faith and they didn't give up.

And then Rasool Allah ﷺ says; there was a woman with her child in her arms, an infant and she was walking towards the fire but then she hesitated,

imagine a mother carrying her infant.

So, she hesitated for a while and then Rasool Allah ﷺ says; but the infant spoke and said: O mother, be patient because you are following the true path.

And she jumped in the fire.

Rasool Allah ﷺ says, there are three, who spoke in young age, this infant was one of them.

This story was recorded in Surat Ul Burooj(سورة البروج), Surat Ul Buruj(سورة البروج) is referring to this story.

Surat Ul Buruj(سورة البروج) talks about the ones, who are burned, As'haab Bil Ukhdood(أصحاب الأخدود) the people of the trench.

Now, even though these people were burned alive, and they ceased to exist, and the king won.

But Allahسبحانه وتعالى said that the Muslims were victorious.

Now, that's interesting.!

These people were killed, they did not establish any Khilafah(خِلَافَه), the king won.

How come, Allahسبحانه وتعالى said: Allahسبحانه وتعالى did not only call it victory, Allah said that is the great victory.

Why?

How come these people lost in terms of worldly standards.?

Nevertheless, they're still called victorious.

Victory in their regard is the fact that they were able to hold firm on their faith until, the last moment, they never gave up.

That is victory entering Jannah(جنة) is victory.

So, even though they did not survive in Duniyah(دُنِيَّا), but they were able to hold firm on their religion.

So, the father of Ammar Yasir(عمار ياسر) has won, Sumayyah(سميعه) has won, Hamza Bin Abdul Muttalib(حمزه بن عبدالمطلب), even though he was killed in the battlefield, he has won.

They have won in the eternal sense of winning, even though they might have lost in a temporary battle in Duniyah(دُنِيَّا).

But the eternal battle they have won it, because they have entered Jannah(جنة), and Allahسبحانه وتعالى says: that is the great victory.

There is one person, who survived.

And this person traveled all the way to visit the Roman Emperor.

Now, he went to the Roman Empire because the Roman Empire was Christian, even though these two people would be different Christian sects, because by that time, the Romans might have already adopted the Trinity and the divinity of Eesa(عيسى).

But they still considered themselves to be followers of Eesa(عيسى).

So, he went to seek help from the Roman Emperor.

He said, this is what happened to us, we were persecuted, we were killed.

We need your help.!

The Roman Emperor said: We are too far from Yemen.

But what, I could do, is send a message to the Najjashi(نجاشي), the Nagus, of Abyssinia, who's also a Christian, and he can help you.

So, the Roman Emperor did that.

And they sent the message to An-Najjashi(ألنجاشي), in English, the Nagus.

And he sent an army led by a general named Ar-Rayyat(أرياط) and Ar-Rayyat(أرياط) invaded Yemen, and fought with Du Nawaas(ذو نواس), and Du Nawaas(ذو نواس), when he lost, he committed suicide.

It says that he was on his horse, and he just jumped in, to the Red Sea, he killed himself.

So, he lost, and now the Abyssinians were ruling over parts of Yemen.

And they did this as a revenge for the Christians, who were killed by the Jews of Yemen.

Ar-Rayyat(أرياط) ruled over Yemen for a while, he was very strict.

One of his army generals staged a revolt against him, and the Abyssinians in Yemen, were divided now, a group of them were with Ar-Rayyat(أرياط),

and the other group were with the new leader called Abraha(أبرهة).

And they were fighting, Ar-Rayyat(أرياط) told Abraha(أبرهة); If we kill each other, the people of the land will take over.

So, how about we have a one-on-one fight, a man to man, Me and You.

Abraha(أبرهة) agreed.

But Abraha(أبرهة) made a secret agreement with some of his security guards.

That if you see me losing, jump in and help, if you see me winning, leave me alone.

If you see that I'm losing come in.

So, you have all these people surrounding and Abraha(أبرهة) and Ar-Rayyat(أرياط) are in the middle, now Ar-Rayyat(أرياط) was described as a tall and thin man,

and Abraha(أبرهة) was short and chubby.

So, Ar-Rayyat(أرياط) he was able to strike Abraha(أبرهة) from the top and he chopped off his nose.

So, Abraha(أبرهة) was called Abraha Al-Ushrum (أبرهة ألأشرم), Ashram(اشرم), means his nose is chopped off.

When that happened, the bodyguards jumped in and they killed Ar-Rayyat(أرياط).

He betrayed obviously this is against rules, but the issue is over now, Ar-Rayyat(أرياط) is dead.

Abraha(أبرهة) now took over and he was the one, ruling over Yemen.

Abraha(أبرهة) wanted to change the religion of the people, and forced them to become Christian.

And since the Arabs were attached to Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), he decided to build a counterpart to Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) in Sana'a(صنعاء), in Yemen.

So, he built a huge Cathedral called Al-Kulais(ألكليس).

And this was described as a wonderful piece of art and huge, and great.

I mean, he had access of wealth from Abyssinia.

So, they built this huge Cathedral in Sana'a(صنعاء) to compete with Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

Now, one man didn't like this idea.

What he did was a bit crude.

He went into Al-Kullais(ألكليس), and he defecated and then not only that, he took it and he spread it all over the walls stool, imagine stool all over the walls, and he ran away.

Abraha(أبرهة) was furious.

What is this, what is this guy doing?

He was so angry, he decided that he must get rid of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

I mean, I'm going to put an end to this, and destroy Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), he mobilized an army and the march towards Makkah.

There was some resistance along the way, one of the chiefs of a tribe, his name is Nufail(نفيل).

He put up some resistance, but he was defeated, I mean Abraha(أبرهة) is a huge powerful army.

And they captured Nufail(نفيل), they captured him as a prisoner of war.

When Abraha(أبرهة) reached to At-Taef(ألطائف), the people of At-Taef(ألطائف) assisted Abraha(أبرهة), and one of them offered to be a guide for Abraha(أبرهة), for the rest of the journey.

And this man his name is Abu Raghal(أبو رغال).

So, Abu Raghal(أبو رغال), he went out to the army.

But then immediately when they got out of At-Taef(ألطائف) he died.

So, then the Arabs were so upset with Abu Raghal(أبو رغال) they built in the place of his death a monument that they would stone, because of his betrayal.

Anyway, Abraha(أبرهة) made it to the outskirts of Makkah And there were some shepherds with camels, grazing He took possession of them.

200 of these camels belonged to Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) the grandfather of Rasool Allah ﷺ.

So, Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) came out of Makkah to meet with Abraha(أبرهة).

Now obviously, Abraha(أبرهة), you can't just walk in and meet him, he was such a important figure.

So, Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) has to have some connections to get in, Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) happened to be a friend of Nufail(نفيل).

Who was captured as a prisoner of war.

Nufail(نفيل) was carried with the army.

And he befriended, he became friends with a man called Unais(أنيس).

And this man Unais(أنيس) was such an important person in the army.

He was a pilot of the elephant, which was their most valuable, piece of equipment.

So, Nufail(نفيل) now is very well connected, he knows Unais(أنيس).

So, Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) came to Nufail(نفيل) and told him; I want to meet with Abraha(أبرهة).

Nufail(نفيل) told him: Sure, I'll arrange for your a meeting through my friend Unais(أنيس).

So, Unais(أنيس) arranged the meeting with Abraha(أبرهة).

And Abraha(أبرهة) welcomed Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب).

Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) walked in, and Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) was described as being a man with a very strong presence in all.

I mean, by just seeing him, a person becomes impressed.

So, when Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) came in, Abraha(أبرهة) held him, in a high esteem, even though they didn't even talk yet.

Now, the rules were that Abraha(أبرهة) sits on a very high throne.

And people sit under his feet.

So, you come and have a meeting with Abraha(أبرهة), you are sitting under his feet.

Abraha(أبرهة), when he saw Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب), he didn't feel comfortable at all, having Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) sit under him.

But he cannot also allow Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) to sit with him, on the throne because nobody should sit on the throne, except he.

So, what he did is he came down from his throne and sat with Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) on the floor.

And he told Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب), he told the interpreter to ask Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب), what does he need?

Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) straight ahead, told the interpreter.

Abraha(أبرهة) has taken possession of 200 of my camels, I want them back.

Abraha(أبرهة) responded and said: When I saw you, I had so much respect for you, but I've lost it all.

I'm coming to destroy your honor and the honor of your father's, I am coming to destroy the center of your livelihood, I am coming to destroy Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), and you're asking me about camels.

Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) responded and said: I am the owner of the camels.

So, I'm responsible for them.

And this house belongs to Allah and Allah will protect it.

I'm here to ask for what is under my authority, my responsibility.

The house belongs to Allah, Allah will take care of it and Allah will protect it.

Abraha(أبرهة) said give him back his camels.

Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) went back to Makkah and he told the people of Makkah, do not fight, withdraw out of Makkah, Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) gave them clear instructions.

We're not going to fight Abraha(أبرهة), we're going to leave.

And they all went up to the mountains.

And Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) was the last one to leave and before he left, he was hanging on the clothes of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) or the handle of the door of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

And he was praying to Allahسبحانه وتعالى to protect His house, and then he left.

So, all of them have evacuated, everyone evacuated Makkah.

And Abraha(أبرهة) now issued his instructions to march forth.

But the elephant refused to move.

They turned the elephant to a different direction, he would stand up running.

They turned him towards the direction of Makkah, he would sit down.

How come, a miracle from Allah but it is said in the story, that this man Nufail(نفيل), who was a prisoner of war, he released himself from his chains,

and he jumped to the ear of the elephant and he said to the elephant, this is the house of Allah, do not attack it and he ran away.

But whether that was the reason or not, the elephant refused to march in the direction of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), and they would beat it, they started poking it with their spears,

and the elephant was bleeding, it refused to move.

Eventually, they decided they're gonna have to leave the elephant and they made their move forward.

Allahسبحانه وتعالى sent on them an army.

No, one knows the soldiers of Allah, anything can be a soldier of Allah.

Water which is the source of life can be a soldier of Allah.

Water is, what killed the tyrant, Firoun(فرعون).

Wind is a soldier of Allah, Allahسبحانه وتعالى says; No one knows His soldiers but He.

So, Allahسبحانه وتعالى sent an army of birds, every birds carrying with it, missiles, that were sent on the army of Abraha(أبرهة) and destroy them all, they were all killed.

And this event was recorded in Surat Tul Feel(سورةالفيل).

These are the events up to the year, in which Rasool Allah ﷺ was born.

Rasool Allah ﷺ was born in the year of the elephant, in the same year, Rasool Allah ﷺ was born.

فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُولٍ۝

صَلَّى الله عَلى سَيَّدِنَا محمد وَعَلى اَلِهِ وَ صَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ

parts.english:
The Life Of Muhammadﷺ, The Makkan period by Imam Anwar Al-Awlaki.

Yesterday we talked about the importance of studying Seerah(سيرة).

And now we'll start with the first session on Seerah(سيرة), itself.

Now usually the authors or the scholars, who write about the life of Muhammadﷺ, they do not usually start talking about his birth.

They would go a little bit before that, actually about few thousand years before that and they would talk about his father Ibrahim عليه السلام.

That's usually where they would start talking about Rasool Allah ﷺ, they would talk about his ancestry, starting by Ibrahim عليه السلام.

The emphasis is on the Hajar(هاجر) and Ismail(اسماعيل) side of the story rather than the, Is'haaq(اسحاق) and Sarah(ساره), because that's the lineage of Muhammadﷺ.

So, they would start by talking about the story of Ibrahim علبه السلام, Hajar(هاجر) and Sarah(ساره), when they traveled to Hijaz(حجاز).

Ibrahim عليه السلام, his wife and his newborn son, traveled into Arabia, into the land of Hijaz(حجاز).

And Ibrahim(ابراهيم) took them to present day Makkah.

At that time, there was nothing there, nobody was living there, there was no cultivation.

It was a dead Valley.

But the place where the House of Allah is built, the place where the Al-Ka'aba(الكعبه) was built was sacred, since the world was created.

In fact, there's a difference of opinion on who is the first one to build Al-Ka'aba(الكعبه).

The majority opinion is that it was Ibrahim عليه السلام but there are some scholars, who say that Adam(آدم) was the first one to build it.

Now, regardless of whether Ibrahimعليه السلام or Adamعليه السلام built it, the place itself, whether there was a building on it or not, was holy and sacred from day one.

Ibrahim عليه السلام and his wife and son, arrived to the valley and in the place where Zam-Zam(زمزم) is currently, obviously there wasn't Zam-Zam(زمزم) at that time.

Ibrahim عليه السلام left his wife and son, Ismael(اسماعيل).

He left with them some water and a leather bag of dates.

And he walked away.

He just turned away and left.

Now, Hajarعليها السّلام knew that Ya'ani(يعني) Ibrahimعليه السلام was gonna leave them but she didn't expect to be left in such a place, in the middle of the desert.

So, she followed him and she said: Ibrahim(اِبْراهِيْم)! Are you gonna leave us in a place where there's no cultivation and there's no one living.?

Ibrahim عليه السلام did not answer back.

She asked him again, no response, she asked him a third time, he didn't answer back, and then Hajarعليها السّلام said: Did Allah tell you to do so?.

Ibrahimعليه السلام said: Yes.

Then Allah will take care of us.

If this is a command from Allah, then I have trust in Allah that He will take care of us.

Look at the faith of this woman, in the middle of nowhere.

But if this is the command of Allah, I have trusted in Allah, Allah will take care of us.

Allah will not waste us, Allah will not neglect us.

Ibrahim عليه السلام left and when he reached to a place where they cannot see him anymore.

Ibrahimعليه السلام turned around and faced Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) or the place of Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه).

And he made Dua(دُعَا) to Allah.

He said: Ibrahimعليه السلام said: O Allah, I'm leaving my offspring, in infertile land, a land where there is, no cultivation.

Next to your sacred house.

So, the place was known that it was sacred even though Al-Ka'aba(الكعبه) wasn't built.

And then Ibrahimعليه السلام made a Dua(دُعَا).

Now, you know the Maslow hierarchy of needs, the pyramid?

What is the foundation of the pyramid?

The bottom!

What is the first human need that needs to be satisfied?

What does it start with?

First thing is what?

Physiological needs, right?

That's the bottom of the pyramid.

So, that is the most important need for humans.

That's the base of the pyramid.

And then what's after that, what's the next step, Psychological, and then the third, Social, Physiological on the bottom, Social, Spiritual,

and then the peak is, Self-actualization.

So, that's the pyramid.

First of all, as a human being you want to satisfy the physiological necessary needs which are food and shelter.

After that, you want to have friends, have a social life, have a belonging, an Association.

So, those are the social needs, and then you have the spiritual needs.

So, after you have achieved the physiological needs and the social needs after that, you start thinking about religion, according to Maslow.

Finally, you have the self-actualization, which is on the top of the pyramid.

But according to Ibrahimعليه السّلام, the pyramid is inverted.

The first thing that he asked for was not food and drink or shelter.

The first thing he asked for, was: The first thing that they asked for even though it would make sense that they would ask for...

I mean, we would assume that Ibrahimعليه السّلام, since he left them in a valley where there's, there's no cultivation, the first thing he would ask for is to provide his family with food, for their survival.

But Ibrahimعليه السلام started in his Dua(دُعَا) by saying; O Allah so that, they may establish prayer.

So, the first need that he asked for, or the first thing that he mentioned, was spiritual needs, Salah(صلاة), Establishing the prayers and then he said:

And then make or put their love, in hearts of people.

Ya'ani(يعني) make people love them.

So, he is asking Allahسبحانه وتعالى to draw people to his family, and to make them love his family.

So, he's asking for the social needs, and then finally he said: Then provide them with fruits.

So, Ibrahimعليه السلام is starting by asking for Salah(صلاة), spiritual needs and then social needs and then physiological needs.

But even when he asked Allahسبحانه وتعالى to provide them with Samaraat(ثمرات), fruits, he also connected it, to Ibadah(عبادة) and said: So, that they may be grateful.

So, even when he was asking Allah to provide them with worldly things, he was still connecting it to religion.

Give them fruit, so that they will be grateful to you.

And that is true self-actualization, when Allah becomes everything for you.

When you're eating, when you're drinking, when you're sleeping, you're doing everything for Allah.

That is the true tranquility and that is the self-actualization that neither did Maslow, or anybody else achieve, except the Ambiyaa(أنبِيَاء) of Allah and Aouliyaa(أولياء) of Allahعَزّوجَلّ.

And then Ibrahimعليه السّلام left.

Hajar(هَاجر) made use of the small amount of food that he left with them, but obviously after a short while they ran out of food and Hajarعليها السّلام was breastfeeding Ismail(اسماعيل)

you know, in the tribal societies, your strength is based on how many men you have on your side, and you can only count on your relatives.

That is how life in the desert is.

Your strength is based on how many sons how many men you have with you, how many brothers, how many sons, how many uncles that is your strength.

So, Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) felt weak, he has only one son, on his side, Al-Harris(الحارث).

So, he said, O Allah, if you bestow me with 10 sons, I will sacrifice one of them for Your sake.

And Allahسبحانه وتعالى did bless him with 10 male sons.

He had 10 male sons and six daughters.

So, when he had 10.

Now, it's time for him to fulfill his promise to Allah, that he will sacrifice one of them.

So, they had these arrows next to Hubal(حبل), Hubal(حبل) is, one of their large idols.

And they believe that these arrows were divine, so they would cast lots and they would leave their choices, they would leave the decision up to the this random way of casting lots.

So, Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) had the name of every one of his 10 sons on these arrows.

So, it came one who.?

Abdullah(عبدالله), he did it a second time it came on Abdullah(عبدالله), third time it came on Abdullah(عبدالله).

So, Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) took his son Abdullah(عبدالله) with him, right next to the Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) and he was ready with a knife to slaughter him.

Abu Talib(ابوطالب), one of the elder sons of Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) went to his father and said, We cannot allow you to kill your son.

And then the maternal relatives of Abdullah(عبدالله) came and said, we're not going to allow you to kill our son.

And people were coming in and they were telling Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب), if you do it, then it will become Sunnah(سنة) for the Arabs after you.

Because Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) was their leader.

So, if he did something, it would become a trend after that.

And they said, if you do it, then any one of us, after that to us 10 sons will follow your footsteps.

And we will be killing each other.

I mean, they were already killing their daughters, and now they will start killing their sons.

So, they insisted on Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) not to do it.

Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) told them this was a pledge that I did to Allah.

I cannot give it up, I cannot break my promise.

They told him, No, you have to stop it.

Anyway, they had to dispute.

How can they solve this dispute?

Let's go to the witch.

So, they decided to go and visit the witch again.

They went to the witch and they told her, this is the situation.

She said, All right, come back to me tomorrow, so that I can consult my spirits, this evening.

Tonight, I'll speak to the Jinn.

They came back the next day and she had an answer for them.

She told them.

What is the retribution that you pay, to a person that was killed?, Diya(دية), the blood money, how much is it?

They said 10 camels.

She said then put 10 camels on one side and put Abdullah(عبدالله) on the other side and cast a lot.

If it points towards the camels, then slaughter the camels, if it points towards Abdullah(عبدالله), then add another 10 camels.

So, they agreed and they went back, so Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) with all of the people of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ), they came together, Abdullah(عبدالله) on one side, the camels on the other side, they threw the dice or the arrows

it pointed towards Abdullah(عبدالله).

They added another 10 camels.

It's pointed towards Abdullah(عبدالله), added another 10.

So, now we're up to 30, 40, 50, 60, and it's pointing towards Abdullah(عبدالله) all the way, until a 100.

They had 100 camels on one side Abdullah(عبدالله) on the other side, finally it pointed towards the camels.

The people of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) said: Finally, we can release your son Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) said not yet.

We'll have to do it another time.

Cast lots the second time, cast lot the third time, it was consistently pointing towards the camels.

So, he slaughtered the hundred camels and he had to pay for it all.

And Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) was a very generous man, he refused to take any of that meat, he gave it out and there was so much meat, that there was so much and the people would, take so much of it,

but there was still enough to feed the birds and to feed the beasts.

So later on, they would say: Ya'ani(يعني) it became famous among the Arabs that Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) is the one, who fed the humans and the animals.

He's the one who even fed the birds in the sky.

And we'll talk about an incident when this saying was brought up, in a conversation with Abu Bakr(ابو بكر) and one leader of a clan.

Now, the people of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) were right, when they told Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) if you kill your son, it will become a tradition among the Arabs after you,

because when Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب) sacrificed a 100 camels to save his son, the blood money among them changed from 10 camels to 100, because of what happened with Abdul Muttalib(عبد المطلب).

So, the retribution now that is paid was 100 rather than 10.

And by the way, this tradition was kept and reserved by Islam.

So, the Diya(ديعا) is still today 100 camels, however now, they would calculate it in terms of currency, but it is still based on that concept.

This is the story of Abdullah(عبدالله).

Now, Abdullah(عبدالله) and Aamna(آمنه) are the parents of Rasool Allah ﷺ.

Later on, they would tell Muhammadﷺ that you are the son of the two sacrificed ones.

And who are they.?

Who are the two sacrifice one's.?

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ is the son of the two sacrifice ones, his father Abdullah(عبدالله) was sacrificed and his father Ismail عليه السلام was sacrificed.

Abdullah(عبدالله) married Aamna Bint Wahb(آمنه بنت وهب).

And we're done with the ancestry of Rasool Allah ﷺ.

Quraish(قُرَيْشْ).

parts.english:
We ask Allahسبحانه وتعالى to bless this gathering.

We ask Allahسبحانه وتعالى to benefit us, from what we learn.

We ask Allahسبحانه وتعالى to teach us that, which will benefit us.

We ask Allahسبحانه وتعالى to make us of those, who will follow the way of Rasool Allah ﷺ and love him.

And we ask Allahسبحانه وتعالى to make us of those, who will be with him in Jannah(جنة).

First of all, we'll start with definition of Seerah(سيرة).

What does the word Seerah(سيرة) mean?

The word, Seerah(سيرة) has a linguistic meaning and that is a path, and walking is called Sair(سير).

When you walk from one place to another, it says, Saraa Fulaan(سَارَ فُلَانْ).

Fulaan(فلان) is walking, or such as this person is walking.

So, it is the path that a person takes, during their lifetime, that is Seerah(سيرة).

And the Hans Wehr dictionary, gives the translation of the word Seerah(سيرة) as conduct, comportment, demeanor, behavior, way of life, attitude, position, reaction, way of acting and biography.

All of these are meanings of the word Seerah(سيرة).

And Seerah(سيرة) could be the biography of any person, it not necessarily Muhammadﷺ.

However, we have used the word so much with Muhammadﷺ, that when we say Seerah(سيرة), we almost, all the time, are referring to, The Life of Muhammadﷺ.

But you could also say the Seerah(سيرة) of Abu Bakr(ابو بكر), the Seerah(سيرة) of Umar(عمر), the Seerah(سيرة) of so and so.

It is a biography of a person, their life.

So, that's the meaning of the word Seerah(سيرة), it is the life of a person, and in this situation, we're studying the life of the greatest; Muhammadﷺ.

What's the importance of studying Seerah(سيرة)?

Number one; The life of Muhammadﷺ is the history of Islam; you're studying a Concise History of Islam by studying, The Life Of Muhammadﷺ.

His life; in His Seerah(سيرة), we would find situations and incidences that would help us in everything that we would need to know, in our life of Da'wah(دعوة).

So, the life of Muhammadﷺ is really the history of Islam.

We're not just studying the biography of a person, we're studying history of our religion.

Muhammad Ibn Sa'ad Bin Abi Waqas(محمد ابن سعد بن ابي وقاص), - Sa'ad Ibn Abi Waqas(سعد إبن وقاص) is one of Ashra Mubashireen Bil Jannah(عشره مبشرين بالجنة),

he is one of the ten(10), who were given glad tidings of paradise.

His son Muhammad(محمد) says: That our father would teach us the battles of Rasool Allahﷺ, he would teach us the Seerah(سيرة) of Rasool Allah ﷺ

and he would tell us that these are the traditions of your fathers.

So, study them.!

And they used to refer to Seerah(سيرة), as Maghazi(مغازي), Maghazi(مغازي) means the battles, because the latter part of Rasool Allah ﷺ was spent in Maghazi(مغازي).

So, they would use this word Maghazi(مغازي) to refer to, The Whole life of Muhammadﷺ.

And Ali Bin Hussain Ibn Ali Ibn Abi Talib(علي بن حسين ابن علي ابن ابي طالب), the grandson of Ali Ibn Abi Talib(علي ابن ابي طالب), he would say that,

we were taught the Seerah(سيرة) of Rasool Allah ﷺ, like we were taught Qur'an.

That is how important Seerah(سيرة) was for them.

They would study it, like they would study Qur'an.

And that makes sense, because if you want to study the life of Musaعليه السلام, where do we go.?

where do we study it from?

From Qur'an.

If we want to study the life of Eesaعليه السلام, we go to Qur'an.

But if we want to study the life of Muhammadﷺ, His life, even though there are bits and pieces of it, mentioned in Qur'an, but we don't have as much details about the life of Muhammadﷺ in Qur'an, as we have about Musa(موسى).

So, the life of Rasool Allah ﷺ for us, to study it, we go to Seerah(سيرة).

All of the Ambiyaa(أنبياء), their lives were recorded in Qur'an, with the exception of Muhammadﷺ, Muhammadﷺ, his life, we'd learn it from Seerah(سيرة).

So, when we want to learn about the Ambiyaa(أنبياء), we go to Qur'an.

When we want to learn about Muhammadﷺ we go to his Seerah(سيرة).

Again - even though there's some references in Qur'an made to his life.

We'll talk about the influence of Seerah(سيرة), in understanding Quran.

Number two!

The second reason for studying Seerah(سيرة).

It is to develop the proper love of Muhammadﷺ, in our hearts.

Loving Muhammadﷺ is Ibadah(عبادة) It's part of our religion to love Muhammad صلوات الله وسلام عليه, He says: One of you does not attain true faith,

until you love me more than you love your parents, your children and the whole world.

We don't really become true believers, until we love Muhammadﷺ more than anything else.

So, it is part of Islam, to love Muhammadﷺ.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab رضي الله عنه, he came to Muhammadﷺ and said: Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) was very honest and straightforward person,

he went to Rasool Allah ﷺ and said, O Rasool Ullah, I love you more than everything except myself.

I love you more than anyone, except myself.

Rasool Allah ﷺ, told him: Until you love me.

Meaning, you don't really attain the complete faith, until you love me more than your own self.

So, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) came back and said: O Rasool Ullah, now I love you more than my own self.

Rasool Allah ﷺ said: Now, you have attained the complete faith.

The Ummah(امة) today, loves Muhammadﷺ.

If you ask any Muslim, do you love Muhammadﷺ? They would say: Yes!

But the love cannot be very deep and sincere, unless you know the person.

If you have shallow information about someone, you can't really love them a lot.

To love a person, you need to know them more.

And this is especially true with Muhammadﷺ because the more you know him, the more you would be impressed with his personality, the more you would love him.

So, even though Muhammadﷺ among the Ummah(امة) today with the shallow information that the masses of the Muslims have, about him, even though they still love him,

but we cannot truly have deep love to Muhammadﷺ unless we know him.

You know, the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم the more they knew him, the closer they were to him, the more they would love him.

Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص) for example, he was one of the staunchest enemies of Muhammad صلوات الله وسلام عليه.

He was one of the top plotters against Islam.

Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص), he later became a Muslim and when he was passing away, Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص) started weeping, he was crying, on his death bed.

So, his son Abdullah Bin Amr(عبدالله بن عمرو) told him: O my father, didn't Rasool Allah ﷺ give you the glad tidings of this, didn't he give you the glad tidings of that.

I mean, it is reported in Hadith, that Rasool Allahﷺ said: That Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص) has attained faith.

So, this is a witness from Rasool Allahﷺ, that Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص) is a Mo'min(مؤمن), not only a Muslim, but he is the higher level of Mo'min(مؤمن).

So, his son was trying to give his father the glad tidings that you are a true believer.

I mean, Rasool Allahﷺ has given you all of these, glad tidings.

How come you are crying now before, your death.

Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص), he turned around, and he said, I have went through three stages in my life.

At the first stage, the most despised man to me, was Muhammadﷺ.

And my desire was that I could get my hold of him, I could get my hands on him and kill him.

That was my desire, that was my wish, my aspiration to kill Muhammadﷺ.

He says; If I died at that time, I would have definitely been in Hellfire.

He said than Allah put the love of Islam in my heart.

And I went to Muhammadﷺ and I said, O Muhammad(محمد).

I want to become Muslim, extend your hand, so that I can pledge allegiance to you, Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص) says; Muhammadﷺ extended his hand forward,

and I pulled my hand away.

So, Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص), he had Rasool Allahﷺ extend his hand, and when Rasool Allahﷺ was ready to put his hand, in his.

Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص), Pulled his hand away.

Rasool Allahﷺ told him: What's wrong.?

Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص) said: I have a condition to make.

Rasool Allah ﷺ told him: What is your condition.?

He said: My condition is that, you pardon me.

You give me clemency because Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص) knew that what he has done in the past, the great crimes that he committed against the Muslims, is sufficient for his execution.

So, he wanted to make sure that Rasool Allah ﷺ would not hold him accountable for what he did in the past, Rasool Allah ﷺ smiled and he said:

"O Amr(عمرو): Don't you know, that Islam erases everything before it, and Hijrah(هجرة) erases everything before it, and Hajj(حج), erases everything before it."

Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص) said: So, I became Muslim.

He said at that stage, Muhammadﷺ, who was my worst enemy, became the most beloved person to me in the world.

He said: And I loved him so much, and I respected him so much, I couldn't even get a full glimpse of his face.

Whenever, I would see him, I would stare downwards.

He said: I have so much love, and respect for him, I couldn't even get a full glimpse of his face, and if you would ask me today, to describe him to you, I couldn't.

He said: and if I died during that stage.

I would have hoped to be in Jannah(جنة).

And then he said, and then later on, came things and we don't know, where we stand?

Anyway, there's some other parts for the Hadith(حديث) but the part that concerns us now is that Amr Bin Aas(عمرو بن العاص) when he got to know Muhammadﷺ, when he became close to him.

Muhammadﷺ, who was his worst enemy became his most beloved friend.

Sohail Bin Amr(سهيل بن عمرو), was sent by Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) to negotiate with Muhammadﷺ before Sulh-Hal-Hudaubiyah(صلح الحديبيه) Sohail Bin Amr(سهيل بن عمرو) was, an international negotiator,

he has been to the courts of the Persian Emperor, the Roman Emperor, the Emperor of Abyssinia.

He's a well connected man.

And now, Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) sent him to negotiate with Muhammadﷺ.

So he went into Madina and he came in and he had firsthand experience with, how the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم treat Muhammadﷺ.

So, Sohail Bin Amr(سهيل بن عمرو) went back to report, to Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) He told them, He said: I've visited the Roman Emperor, I've visited the Persian Emperor,

I've visited An-Najashi(نجاشي) of Abyssinia, but I have never in my life, seen a leader that is so loved by his followers and so much respected by his followers, like Muhammadﷺ.

I have seen nothing like it, in the world.

The Roman Emperor, the Persian Emperor, An-Najashi(نجاشي) of Abyssinia, even though they have all of the power and strength and empires.

I have never seen a people, love their leader so much like the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم loved Muhammadﷺ.

He said: I saw amazing things.

Muhammadﷺ would we making Wudhoo(وضؤ) and the Sahabah(صحابہ) would be rushing to grab the water dripping from his body.

So, he told them: Do whatever you want, these are people, who will never give up their leader.

The Sahabah(صحابه), they will never give him up.

They would give their lives, first.

They would sacrifice everything for him.

So, if you want to love Muhammadﷺ, we need to learn more about him.

I've already said that even though among the masses of Muslims, we don't have much information about Muhammadﷺ, we don't know a lot about his Seerah(سيرة)

because it's not part of the curriculum that schools in the Muslim world teach.

Nevertheless, even though we are ignorant about him and his life.

He is still the most beloved figure that ever lived in humanity.

His name is the most common name in the world.

How many people in the world, are named Muhammad(محمد).

There is no other person that ever lived in history that had so many people named themselves after him like Muhammadﷺ.

When I was in college in the U.S., we had an Imam(إمام), he was from Nigeria, and he was a Hafidh(حافظ) and he was our Imam in the small college town, in the U.S.

And his name was Muhammad Al-Ashr(محمد العشر) Now, the word Ashr(العشر) means the tenth.

So, for a long time, I assumed that Ashr(العشر) is his last name, Muhammad Al-Ashr(محمد العشر).

One day I went up to him and I said, What is Al-Ashr(العشر).?

I mean, is that the name of the tribe or the clan.

He said: No!

He said: My father would name, every male, boy, that he has Muhammad(محمد), all of his children he would name them Muhammad(محمد).

So, to distinguish between us, he has to number us.

So, there was Muhammad, the first Muhammad the second, Muhammad the third, and I'm Muhammad the tenth.

I mean, his father doesn't want to deal with any other name, all of his children are gonna be Muhammad.

And in Pakistan and India you'd, Muhammad Haroon, Muhammad Sulayman, Muhammad Adam, Muhammad, everybody is Muhammad.

There's no one in history that had an Ummah(امة) love him, like the Ummah(امة) loves Muhammadﷺ.

He is the most beloved figure in history.

Now, what will be the situation if we study about his life.

I mean, how much love do we have, then for Muhammad صلوات الله وسلام عليه.

His name is the most frequently mentioned name.

Around the clock, there will be a Mu'azana(مؤذنه), a minaret, that is calling to prayer and mentioning the name of Muhammadﷺ, around the clock.

Because Muslims now are worldwide.

So, in every time zone, you have Muslims.

So, in every minute of the day, there will be a Mu'azana(مؤذنه) that is saying, His name is mentioned around the clock, and by the way, the name Muhammad(محمد) means the praised one.

And there is no one, who was praised like Muhammadﷺ.

I mean, his name, really fulfilled its meaning.

He is the praised one.

He is always praised, whenever we hear his name, What do we say?

So, we want to develop love of Muhammadﷺ and the way we could do it.?

Is by studying his life, we will love him more, the more we study about him.

Say if it be, that your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your mates, or your kindred, the wealth that you have gained, the commerce in which you fear a decline, or the dwellings in which you delight,

are dearer to you than Allah or His Messenger, or the striving in His cause, then wait until, Allah brings about His decision.

And Allah guides not the rebellious.

So, the Ayah(آية) is stating that our love for Allah and His Messenger and striving in the cause of Allah should be paramount to everything else.

Our fathers, our sons, our brothers, our mates, our kindred, our wealth, everything.

Allah, His Messenger and Islam, should be the dearest thing to every one of us.

Number three, why do we study Seerah(سيرة).?

to follow the way of Muhammadﷺ.

Ibn Hazam (ابن حزم) says: Whoever seeks the preeminence of the Hereafter, the wisdom of this life, the just purpose and the embodiment of morality and character,

let him follow Muhammadﷺ, the Prophet of Allah.

So, Muhammadﷺ is the embodiment of Khuluq(خلق), the perfect character and by studying his Seerah(سيرة), we will be more able to follow his way.

Number four, understanding Qur'an: There are some Ayaat(آيات) in Qur'an, that are independent of the circumstances of the revelation.

Like for example, the Ayaat(آيات) about Al-Aakhirah(الآخرة), Ar-Raqaiq (ألرقائق), these are independent of the circumstances.

But then there are some Ayaat(آيات) that were dealing with events that were happening in the time of Muhammadﷺ.

So, you would have some Ayaat(آيات) revealed prior to an event, some Ayaat(آيات) revealed concurrent with an event, and some Ayaat(آيات) revealed after an event.

Seerah(سيرة) would give us the explanation of these Ayaat(آيات).

Like for example, Surah(سورة) Al-Ahzaab(الاحزاب) many Ayaat(آيات) in Surah Ahzaab(سورة الأحزاب) were revealed regarding the Battle of Ahzaab(ألأحزاب),

many Ayaat(آيات) in Surat-Al-Imram(سورة الإعمران) were relating to events that happened in the time of Rasool Allahﷺ.

So, you have a major section of Surat-Al-Imram(سورة الإعمران), was a dialogue between Muslims and Christians, based on the Christian delegation that came from Najraan(نجران) to visit Rasool Allah ﷺ.

These Ayaat(آيات) were revealed to support Rasool Allah ﷺ in his dialogue with the Christians.

And then you also have the end part, the latter part of Al-Imram(آلعمران) is dealing with Ghazwat Uhud(غزوة احد).

Now, the details of Ghazwa(غزوة) are not mention in Surah(سورة), so how can you understand these Ayaat(آيات)?

By going to Seerah(سيرة).

Number five, His life ﷺ illustrates the methodological steps of the Islamic movement.

Rasool Allah ﷺ went through stages, he went through steps, started by a secret Da'wah(دعوة) and then it became public.

And then later on Jihad(جهاد).

So, it went through stages.

These stages are important for Islamic movements to learn and study.

Munir Ghardaan(مُنِيْر غَرْدَان), he says; And we believe that this methodological progression of the prophet's life is divinely directed, for Allah has guided His Prophet in all of his steps.

And it was not a result of a reaction to emerging circumstances.

So, these events that happened in the life of Rasool Allah ﷺ, were not haphazard.

They were planned by Allahسبحانه وتعالى, so that they would be a guidance for us in our attempts to establish Islam again.

So, it's very important that we look at the stages that Rasool Allah ﷺ went through, and the progression of his Da'wah(دعوة).

Rasheed Ridhaa(رشيد رضا) says; Were it not for the education and training, verbal direction would not suffice, for the Seerah(سيرة), taught them how to be guided by the Qur'an,

and train them to be just and moderate in all matters.

So, we have Qur'an and Sunnah(سنة), our verbal teachings.

But how do we apply these verbal teachings, it is by looking into the application of Rasool Allah ﷺ and Sahabah رضي الله عنهم.

So, they took this verbal, teaching into action.

And that is something that only the Muslims have.

I mean, the followers of all the other Ambiyaa(أنبِيَاء) they have lost trace of the Seerah(سيرة) of their Ambiyaa(أنبِيَاء).

But with us, we know how Qur'an was being practiced.

We know how the Sunnah(سنة) of Rasool Allahﷺ was being practice and applied.

There's an Ayah(آية) in Qur'an, that says that you can continue eating and drinking at night time of Ramadan(رمضان), until the white string is distinguished from the black string.

One of the Sahabah(صحابه) he took this literally, what he did is, he had the string under his pillow.

And he would eat and then he would uncover the string, he would pick up the pillow, he wouldn't see the string.

So, he continued eating.

And he was keep on doing that and then he went to Rasool Allah ﷺ and said: This is what I've done, Rasool Allah ﷺ laughed and he said, it doesn't mean that you take a string in your room and you take a look at it,

it means, the white string, which is the first emergence of light in the horizon, that is what is meant by it.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ this Sahabi(صحابي), how to apply that Ayah(آية).

I mean, because I could be in a dark room with no windows, Alright!

and I have a string with me and it would be noon time, and I still cannot see it and I'm continuing to eat.

So, the application of the Ayaat(آيات) and the Ahadith(احاديث) of Rasool Allah ﷺ are shown to us in the life of Muhammadﷺ, and the life of the Sahabah(صحابه), may the blessings and pleasure of Allah سبحانه وتعالى be with them all.

Number Six, Studying Seerah(سيرة) is Ibadah(عبادة), We are not doing this to entertain ourselves.

This is Ibadah(عبادة), there is Ajar(اجر), there is reward in studying this.

We are worshipping Allah by coming together and studying the life of Muhammadﷺ.

This is a Halaqah(حلقه) of Zikr(زكر), this is a session of Zikr(ذكر) when we come together and talk about Muhammadﷺ, we are worshipping Allahسبحانه وتعالى,

and we expect that this is a gathering that will be surrounded by angels, in which Allahسبحانه وتعالى will shower us with His mercy and tranquility and be mentioned in a gathering better than this.

So, it is Ibadah(عبادة) and Allahسبحانه وتعالى says: If you do love Allah, follow me, meaning follow Muhammad ﷺ, Allah will love you and forgive you, your sins.

For Allah is Aft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Number seven, Developing a Muslim identity, brothers or sisters, there is a global culture, that is being forced down on the throats of everyones on the face of the earth,

this global culture is protected and promoted.

Thomas Friedman, he's a famous writer in the U.S., he writes for the New York Times.

He says; The Hidden Hand of the market cannot survive without a hidden fist.

McDonald's will never flourish without McDonnell Douglas, the designer of the F15 (F-Fifteens).

You either accept McDonald's, otherwise McDonnell Douglas will send their F15s above your head.

It's a very intolerant culture that cannot coexist with anything else.

It uproots, every other culture on the face of the earth.

It just cuts the roots of it.

And you have a quote here by Alexander Solzhenitsyn.

He's a famous Russian historian and writer, he says, to destroy a people, you must first sever their roots.

So, it's really a destruction of the people of the earth, because every other culture is being demolished.

So, this is not a global culture that will coexist with others, it will replace others.

And the only ideology that is standing up, against this global culture is Islam.

But still, as Muslims, and especially Muslims living in the West, we are suffering from a serious identity crisis.

I mean, you would find that even though the brother or sister would be practicing Islam, but the identity itself, the Islamic identity itself is lost

I mean, the person would have more in common with a rock star or soccer player, than they would have with the companion of Rasool Allah ﷺ.
