So that's the transformational power that Eeman(ايمان) should have.

So Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) is saying that I want you to give me authority and I will do it.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه did give Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) that authority and he started out the conquest in Iraq.

There was a member of his people, this was a big tribe Bannu Shaiban(بنوشعيبان) and they belong to Rabiyyah(ربيعة), one of them, his name is Mad'oor Bin Udae(مذعور بن عدي)

he was competing with Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) over the position of leading the effort.

And he sent a letter to Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه and he said; We are Ahlaas Al-Khail(أحلاس ألخيل), Ahlaas Al-Khail(أحلاس ألخيل) means, we're stuck to the backs of our horses.

In other words, we ride our horses so much we're so trained in it, we're so good at it.

We're Fursan As-Sabah(فرسان ألصباح), and we are the Knights of the morning.

We attack our enemies early in the morning, and I have men with me, each one of them is equal to a 100.

And he is asking Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) to appoint him as a leader over the Army's in that area.

So now Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) is dealing with a situation where he already appointed Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) and here's somebody else asking for the same position.

And Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) sent a letter to Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) saying that there's a man from my people who contended with me and try to take away my position or compete with me

in this role that you have appointed me to.

So, I just wanted to let you know about it.

Now, Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه is dealing with the realities of life.

You know, there are some interpersonal issues there are… it happens.

It happens even among Muslims, Muslims are not angels.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه he knows, how to run Jama'ah(جماعة) he knows how to manage the affairs of the social life of people and this is part of the ability of the leader.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه to solve this issue because he was already sending in Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) to lead the entire enterprise.

He sent a letter to Mad'oor(مذعور), telling him I take your word for it, what you said.

Even though it might have been an exaggeration of his abilities Allah Ho Alam(ألله أعلم).

He said: I take your word for what you said and I believe you and I'm asking you to join hands with Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and to be with him and to follow him, wherever he goes.

Rather than put Mad'oor(مذعور) and Muthanna(مثنى) in the same.

I mean, he could have told Mad'oor(مذعور) to go under the leadership of Muthanna(مثنى), whom I already appointed, he could have done that and some complications could have came out of that situation.

He said: No! You go with Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد).

So he separated between the two.

Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) is leading an army and Mad'oor(مذعور) with his group are following the leadership of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد)

and nobody can contest the leadership with Khalid(خالد).

They all agree to the ability and the leadership of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) I mean, Sahabah(صحابه) of Rasool Allah ﷺ, who are earlier in Islam than him would all admit

that Khalid Ibn Walid رضي الله عنه is the most capable among us, in leading Armies.

What was the plan of Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق)?

Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) played a role for some time.

But now, Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) wants to have a greater enterprise in the area of Iraq.

So his plan was to send two armies, one army to attack from the south east and the second army to attack from the northwest.

The army that would attacked from the south east was the army of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and he sent him a letter saying go on towards Iraq.

Because Khalid(خالد) was in Al-Yamamah(أليمامة) he just finished off the Harb(حرب) with was Musailimah Al-Kazzab(مسيلمة ألكذاب).

Go on towards Iraq, until you enter it began with the gateway to India, which is Al-Ubullah(ألأبلَّى), they used to call the area of Al-Basra(ألبصرة), they used to call it the gateway to India,

because anybody traveling to India would go through the Persian sea.

So they would call it the gateway to India, he said: And start from the gateway to India and Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله) it is interesting as if Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه is seeing the map in front of him.

When there were no maps, in their hands.

He said: So you enter from the gateway to India, which is Al-Ubullah(ألأبلَّى) render that people of Persia and those nations under their rule peaceable.

And then he sent an army from the northwest, under the leadership of Ayyad Bin Ghanam(عياض بن غنم), one of the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم and he told him to attack from Al-Musayikh(ألمصيخ) which is the North West.

And then look at this strategic sense of Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق).

He said: You both start attacking inwards into Iraq and try racing towards Al-Heira(ألحيرة) and whoever gets to Al-Heira(ألحيرة) first is the Ameer(أمير) over the other one.

Al-Heira(ألحيرة) was midway between Al-Ubullah(ألأبلَّى) and Al-Musayikh(ألمصيخ).

And Al-Heira(ألحيرة) is in a very strategic position.

It is very close to Al-Madain(ألمدائن) which is the capital of the Persian Empire, but it's towards the Arabian Peninsula side.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه wanted them to set base in a Al-Heira(ألحيرة).

So, the two armies attack from the north and the south.

They meet in Al-Heira(ألحيرة), they joined together and then they make their final hit at the Capital, which was a very strategic plan.

This is his letter, he said: When you have joined each other at Al-Heira(ألحيرة), have broken the defenses of Persia and are sure that the Muslims will not be attacked from behind.

Let one of you cover the Muslims and his comrade by staying at Al-Heira(ألحيرة).

Let the other attack Allah's enemy and your enemy in their own house and the abode of their power, Al-Madain(ألمدائن).

Masaleh Kisra(مصالح كسرى), the army base of Kisra(كسرى) was towards the south.

So it was the job of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) to take care of the army basis, and Ayyad Bin Ghanam(عياض بن غنم) will come from the desert side

and descend south, until they meet in Al-Heira(ألحيرة), whoever reaches Al-Heira(ألحيرة) first leads the other and then one of you stays behind and protects the rear of the army

and the other should make a move towards Al-Madain(ألمدائن), the capital of the Persian Empire.

A word on this, Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه wanted to hit the capital and bring an end to the Persian Empire.

Islam does not recognize a government that does not rule by the Hukm(حكم) of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ, but Islam does allow the existence of other religions in the form of Ahluz-Zimmah(أهل الذمة).

So there is tolerance of Ahluz-Zimmah(أهل الذمة) people following another religion, but the rule should belong to Allah over all the earth.

So there's no recognition at all, in Islam to any disbelieving government.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) wants to hit the Persian Empire at its capital and bring an end to it and it was a very ambitious plan,

especially that Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه has just finished off Harb Ar-Riddah(حرب الردَّة) and immediately he is sending out these two armies

and he's not telling them just to take the outskirts.

He's saying: You go straight to Al-Madain(ألمدائن).

Now in his letter, he said; Render the people of Persia and those nations under their rule peaceable.

It was a Persian Empire, not all of the people were Persian, there were some Arabs.

there were some different races because their rule covered a major part of Asia.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه was saying; Render these people peaceful, try to attract them towards Islam, which is a very different message than he was giving to his leaders regarding Al-Murtaddeen(ألمرتدين),

with Al-Murtaddeen(ألمرتدين) he was saying: Whoever lands in your hands, finish them off.

But here he is saying try to attract them, try to bring them close to Islam because the objective of this war is completely different than the objective of the wars of Riddah(ردَّة).

The wars of Riddah(ردَّة) was intended to bring back Muslims back to the rule of Islam.

While these are wars against people, who have not harmed the Muslims, have not conspired against them.

So now Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه is getting into territories that didn't harm the Muslims.

they didn't break any Muslim law or anything, this was a war for Da'wah(دعوة) the purpose of it was Da'wah Ilallah(دعوة الى الله).

So he's saying, when you get into Persia, try to attract the commoners to Islam, try to bring them closer to the folds of the religion.

So you can see that Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) is dealing with a different standard, with Harub Ar-Riddah(حروب الردَّة) and these wars of conquest which are done for the sake of Da'wah(دعوة), calling the people to Allah.

He also told the Armies call to arms those who fought against the apostates and those who have remained steadfast to Islam after the Prophet,

do not let anyone who had apostasized campaign with you, until I give my opinion.

Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) is giving clear instructions to his generals that you should not allow any of the former Murtaddeen(مرتدين) to join in your armies,

even though they're now Muslim, but they shall not fight with you.

Why would Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه do that?

When, he is in great need for as much reinforcements as he can.

Allah Ho Alam(ألله أعلم) but what you could say is that Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه, did not want people who have given up Islam at one point of time, join in armies

because maybe their intention would not be pure.

These are wars of Jihad(جهاد) Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله) these are not wars for booty, these are not wars for expansion this is not a war for pride, these are not wars to oppress others

this is to bring the people to Islam.

So people who have formerly given up Islam, how could they go out and invite the people to it?

Even though they were Muslim today, and then he said; Until I make a decision otherwise, so he wants to wait.

Therefore, none of the people who participated in the Riddah(ردَّة) were allowed to join in the Muslim armies.

To add to the complication of the situation, he sends them a letter telling them, And do not force anyone to go along with you.

From the original soldiers that you had, from the people who were Muslim if they don't want to go along, don't force them to go along, because this is a voluntary war, this is not a defensive war, this is an offensive war.

Therefore, it is what is called Jihad At-Talab(جهادألطلب).

There is Jihad At-Talab(جهادألطلب), and Jihad Ad-Dafah(جهادألدفع).

Jihad Ad-Dafah(جهادألدفع) is when you're defending yourself, this is Fard Aein(فرض عين) on everyone.

But now this Jihad At-Talab(جهادألطلب) you're attacking somebody else's land, therefore it's voluntary, it's not Fard Aein(فرض عين) it's Fard Kifayah(فرض كفاية).

So he told his leaders do not force anyone to go along with you.

So no Murtaddeen(مرتدين) and don't force the Muslims to go, made it difficult.

But Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه saw this as being the most appropriate way to deal with this situation.

Khalid(خالد) asked for reinforcements.

I mean, some of his forces are deserting him.

They're exhausted because of one battle after another, I mean, Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) was described as He would not sleep and not allow anybody to sleep

Friend or Foe, he could keep everyone busy.

I mean, if you look at the record of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد), he's jumping from one battle to another within days.

He's going on from one place to another all over like a tornado.

So obviously, some of his soldiers are having a hard time keeping up with him.

So they start to deserting him, so he's asking for reinforcements.

Who can Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) send?

He doesn't want to force people to go, he doesn't want to allow the Murtaddeen(مرتدين) to join.

So he sends him Al-Qa'Qaa Bin Amr(ألقعقاع بن عمرو), one man.

So, the Khalifah(خليفه) was told.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه said; An army in which there is the like of this man, will not be defeated?

If Al-Qa'Qaa(ألقعقاع) is in an army, don't worry, that army would not lose.

So he sends one man as reinforcement to Khalid Ibn Walid رضي الله عنه.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) gets into Iraq, and he's appointed the general Ameer(أمير) of all of the forces.

So now he has under him 18,000 troops.

So Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد), he sends a message and this was the Sunnah(سنة) of our generals, before war, they would send a letter giving Da'wah(دعوة) to the people.

So he sent a letter to Al-Hurmozan(ألهرمزان), who was in the area of Al-Ubullah(ألأبلَّى), which is very close to Al-Basra(ألبصرى).

He says: I call you to Allah and to Islam.

If you respond to the call, then you are Muslims.

You obtain the benefits they enjoy, and take up the responsibilities, they bear.

If you refuse, then you must pay Jizya(جزية), if you refuse the Jizya(جزية) I will bring against you tribes of people who are more eager for death than you are for life.

We will then fight you until Allah decides between us and you.

Very decisive, clear, to the point, no confusion whatsoever, he sends this letter, Al-Hurmozan(ألهرمزان) refuses and he decides to fight so they go out to the battlefield and it was called Marakah Tis-Salasil(معركة السلاسل), the Battle of the chains.

Because the enemy, the heart is so weak, they have to tie themselves to each other in chains.

So, that they wouldn't run away.

While the Muslims are so eager to die, you want the chain to bring them back, to slow them down.

And these are having chains so that they wouldn't run away.

It was a disastrous defeat for the enemy.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) immediately moves on to Al-Mazar(ألمضار), another defeat to the enemy, Al-Walajah(ألولجة).

When he gets to Al-Walajah(ألولجة) now he's getting into the beautiful places of Iraq in terms of the farmland and the produce.

So Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) he gave a Khut'ba(خطبة) to his troops before the battle.

He said: Can't you see all of the produce of this land?

By Allah! It struggled for Allah's sake, if Jihad(جهاد) for Allah's sake and calling the people to Islam were not required of us, and there were no consideration except our livelihood.

The wise opinion would still have been that we strike this countryside, until we possess it.

And that we leave hunger and decrease whoever stayed behind and didn't join you.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) is looking at this blessed land.

He is saying: If Jihad(جهاد) was not a duty on us, and Da'wah(دعوة) is not a duty on us, just the beauty of this land and the wealth of it, is sufficient enough as a reason to invite us to come here.

And then he said: Let's leave hunger to the ones, To the ones who are clinging behind to the earth.

The ones who don't want to fight in the path of Allah, let's leave the life of poverty to them.

And Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله), even though Jihad(جهاد) is not done for the sake of Ghanimah(غنيمه), it's not done for the sake of booty and livelihood,

but as a reward from Allah, Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ gives them a life of wealth and gives them longer lives.

And the ones, who stay behind Allah makes them die in loads, and they live a life of weakness, despair, humiliation, if we would draw a curve of the number of Muslims, who die during the time of Jihad(جهاد)

and when they stopped Jihad(جهاد) you would find out that when Muslims are fighting, no one dies, a very small number and when they stop, millions died.

So it is actually a protection of life, even though it seems as a way to means to deprive it.

Now Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) is not inviting the people to the It-imaat(إطعمات) or the food that's coming out from the land, he is just telling them that:

I mean, we have a nobler cause, we're not doing it for the sake of Ghanimah(غنيمه).

But Ghanimah(غنيمه) comes as a byproduct of our struggle Ghanimah(غنيمه) comes as a byproduct.

And the scholars have talked about the issue of having the intention of fighting for the sake of Allah and also fighting for the sake of Ghanimah(غنيمه).

Some scholars approve that intention and some of them say: No!

The intention should be purely for the sake of fighting.

But this again, an issue of Fiqh(فقه). We're not going to get into.

Another defeat of the enemy.

I mean with Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد), it's redundance.

I mean, we're going to keep on saying that he won, he won, he won.

Because that's all what happened to him, he never really lost, at all.

In the next battle, Ulais(أليس) and Amkeshia(أمكيشية).

Again, he defeated the enemy and a great number of them were killed in that battle.

So all of this news was getting to Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) one victory after another.

So, Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق), he said; O people of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ): Your lion has attacked the enemy's lion and overcome him, taking away the pieces of his prey.

And then he says: Women are incapable of ever giving birth to the like of Khalid(خالد).

Women cannot give birth to a man like this.

So now they reached to Al-Heira(ألحيرة).

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) wasn't only good at fighting, but he was very good at diplomacy and he would succeed in many occasions, in having people give up and surrender without a fight.

So he talks to the four chiefs of the major castles or forts in Al-Heira(ألحيرة) and these were Christian Arabs.

So he gives them the three options of becoming Muslim or paying the Jizya(جزية) or fighting.

So, they said: We're gonna pay Jizya(جزية).

Khalid(خالد) told them: May you perish, woe to you.

Disbelief is a desert that makes one lose his way.

It is only the foolish one, among the Arabs, who would follow it.

And this also shows that the intention of Jihad(جهاد) wasn't Jizya(جزية), wasn't money, because the Muslims would be better off, if people didn't become Muslim.

Financially it's better for the government that people do not embrace Islam, because of Jizya(جزية).

So, these people agreed to pay a huge amount of money but Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) told them: Woe to you, may you perish.

Can't you understand, that disbelief is a desert that makes one lose himself.

But they insisted and they said: We don't want to become Muslim.

So, Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد), knows that, For Allah to guide one man through you, is better than a flock of camels.

That's a Hadith(حديث) in Bukhari(بخاريْ).

So they wrote a contract, Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد), he wrote: In the Name of Allah, the all Compassionate, the Merciful.

This is the covenant that Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) has made with so and so, the four names.

Khalid(خالد) has given them a covenant in return for 190,000 Dirham(درهم)s payable annually for the Jizya(جزية) of those working in this world, including their monks and priests,

except for those among them, who have no work cut off from worldly life, or those who are traveling.

In other words, the monks who are in monasteries and living a life of Zuhud(زهد) and devotion and are far away from Duniyah(دُنِيَّا), they don't pay Jizya(جزية).

But the other monks who are practicing a normal life should pay it.

Khalid(خالد) promises them protection.

So you pay Jizya(جزية) and the Muslims promise protection, if he does not protect them, then they have no obligations, until he does protect them.

So if the Muslims cannot protect them, they pay them their money back.

If they commit betrayal indeed or word, then the Muslims conscious is free of any obligation to them.

but he will not be able to function it.

Because Allah has put Wahn(ألوهن) in his heart.

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ talks about the Battle of Rasool Allah ﷺ with Al-Yahood(أليهود), Allah cast fear in their hearts, they had the strongest forts,

but Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ when he put fear in their hearts, their force did not help, their weapons did not help and their numbers did not help.

And Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ is the One, Who controls the hearts and He can put Wahn(ألوهن) or Ro'ub(رعب) in any heart. Rasool Allah ﷺ says: I was given victory a distance of a month through fear.

Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) was now given the sole authority over the forces in Iraq.

So, he was the leader there.

Al-Muthanna Bin Harissa Ash-Shaibani(ألمثنى بن حارثه شعيباني), was such a great leader and general it's a name that you must remember.

He was the one, who played a very important role in Iraq, in opening Iraq and he continued with Al-Fatoohaat(ألفتوحات) in Al-Iraq(ألعراق), in the absence of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد).

So, he needed some reinforcements because he was getting deep into the territory of the enemy.

He sends a letter to Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه.

But Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) was busy with a more important priority at the time and that was the conquest of the Holy Land.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) delayed his response to Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى), he was busy.

When Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) saw that he didn't get back a response from the Khalifah(خليفه).

He decided that he's going to go himself and meet with the Khalifah(خليفه).

So he leaves Iraq and it goes to Madina and he meets with the Khalifah(خليفه) and explains to him the situation, the Khalifah(خليفه) doesn't have anybody to give him.

Al-Khalifah(خليفه) has mobilized and squeezed, the tribes for all of their fighting forces and sent them to the Holy Land.

So Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) said: Then reinforced me with the Muslims, the ex Murtaddeen(مرتدين).

Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) was on his deathbed at that time.

So for his entire Khilafah(خِلَافَه), he has refused to allow Murtaddeen(مرتدين) to join.

Now since things are different, Al-Murtaddeen(ألمرتدين) have stood firm on Islam, he attested them for two years, Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) considered it.

So he told Umar(عُمَر), who was next to him.

He said: O Umar(عُمَر), Listen O Umar(عُمَر) to what I say to you, then act according to it.

I hope to die on this day of mine.

If I die, do not by any means let the evening enter before you have summon the men to go with Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) if I delay, until the night do not by any means,

let the morning come before you summon the men to go with Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى).

Do not let any catastrophe at all even if it is great, keep you from the matter of your religion and your Lord's counsel.

You saw what I did, on the day of the Messenger of Allah.

See Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) is telling Umar(عُمَر): Do not let any catastrophe hold you back from fulfilling your duties towards Allah and His messenger, he's alluding to his death.

He is saying: Even if I die, don't let that hold you back from mobilizing the forces on the same day I die and sending them out with Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى).

Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله) Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) is not even willing to give a break.

And then he said: You saw what I did on the day the Messenger of Allah died and the people were never stricken with the like of it.

I mean, you saw what I did on that day that is when the Khalifah(خليفه) was given Baiyah(بَيْعة) to.

Three days after that I'm sending out the army of Osamah(أسامة).

So the death of Rasool Allah ﷺ was much greater catastrophe than my death.

Did not hold me back from fulfilling my duties.

So I want you O Umar(عُمَر) to follow my way.

Then he says: By Allah! If I were to weaken in the affair of Allah and the affair of His Messenger, He would abandon me and punish me so that Madina would be consumed in fire.

If Allah grants victory to the commanders in Syria.

Return the troops of Khalid(خالد) to Iraq, for they are its people, the governors of its affair alone, and the people of violence and courage against the enemy.

He says: If we finished with the affair of the Holy Land, send the people of Iraq back to Iraq.

That's their land and they are the people of courage and violence against their enemy.

So Al-Muthanna Bin Harissa Ash-Shaibani(ألمثنى بن حارثه شعيباني) was reinforced.
parts.arabic:
اَعُوْذُ بِاللهِ مِنَّ الشِّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيْمِ۝بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَانِ الرَّحِيْمَ۝

اَلْحَمْدُ لله، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلى سَيِّدِنَا محمد وَعَلَى اَلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ تَسْلِيْمًا كَثِيْرًا لقد انقطع الوحي وتم الدين، أينقص وأنا حي؟

"وتم الدين" أَحَسِبَ النَّاسُ أَن يُتْرَكُوا أَن يَقُولُوا آمَنَّا وَهُمْ لَا يُفْتَنُونَ ۝

فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْكَاذِبِينَ۝

أُمِرْتُ أَن أُقاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَشْهَدُوا أَن لا إِلهَ إِلاَّ اللَّه وأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ قَالُواْ إِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ۝

تعلف أهل الفارس ومن كان تحتهم من الأمم "حتى أرَا رائ" ولا تستفتح بمستكرح لا ينام ولا يترك أحد ينام تثاقل عما أنتم عليه فو اللَّهِ لأنْ يهْدِيَ اللَّه بِكَ رجُلًا واحِدًا خَيْرٌ لكَ من حُمْرِ النَّعم

مضَّك الله ملكة "هذا ولله صم الساعة" "بسم الله" ألذي لا يضرُّ ما إسمه شيءٌ في ألسموات والأرض "بسم الله" "وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا"

فسلك الطريق لم يسلقها إنسانٌ قبلهم قط وسارع إلى مكة في طريق لم يسلق قبله قط وتعتله في ذالك أمرٌلم يقعل لغيره فجعل يسير متعصفًا على غير جاد حتى إنتهاء إلى المكة

"حتى ألرضى" قد قاتلت العرب والعجم في الجاهلية والإسلام والله لمائة من العجم في الجاهلية كانوا أشد على من ألف من العرب ولمائة اليوم من العرب أشد على من ألف من العجم ؛ إن الله أذهب مصدوقتهم

، ووهن كيدهم ؛ فلا يروعنكم زهاء ترونه ولا سواد ولا قسي فج ، ولا نبال طوال، فإنهم إذا أعجلوا عنها أو فقدوها، كالبهائم أينما وجهتموها اتجهت ولكن قلوبهم خانتهم حين كان أهج ألناس عليها

وَقَذَفَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعْبَ نصرت بالرعب مسيرة شهر صَلَّى الله عَلى سَيَّدِنَا محمد وَعَلى اَلِهِ وَ صَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ
